text: A HIDDEN GEM!!!!!!!!! I had the Chelo Kabob Barg and Kashke Badenjan!  It was out of this world.  Delicious.  Very nice folks too.   Attached to a store.  Clean and accessible.   Enjoyed the music on the TV.  A wonderful experience!!!!! Can't wait to return!!!!!!

I am half-Iranian and absolutely LOVE Persian cuisine. When I lived in South Florida, I had a number of good restaurants from which to choose... so upon moving here, I was rather dismayed to find only TWO Persian restaurants in the entire Tampa Bay area. Thankfully, Persia House of Kabobs is only about 15 minutes from my house, because the other restaurant (Mirage in Clearwater) is a bit more of a trek.

While this is more of a fast-casual restaurant, the quality of the food is on point. They don't have all of the varieties larger restaurants would have (such as my favorite Persian dish, fesenjan, or my favorite dessert, falloodeh), but their kabobs are very well done.

I usually order the jujeh (chicken) or koobideh (ground beef) kabobs, or they have a combo where you can get one skewer of each. The chicken is marinated and so flavorful, and the beef has a good amount of spices mixed in. And their Persian rice (which I prefer to other styles, it's not sticky since it gets rinsed multiple times before cooking) is pretty good. Each meal also comes with must o'khiar, which is a cucumber yogurt dip with mint and other herbs and spices. It's one of my favorite things to order at any Persian restaurant so I'm happy it's included with the meal! They also include a large pita, although I wish they had lavash bread instead (it's a papery thin bread that I love dipping in the yogurt).

Don't forget to ask for some sumac for your kabobs or rice, they have them in little to-go packets!

The place is very outdated but please give them a chance!! DELICIOUS food!! We had the Jujeh (Chicken) plate and the beef and koobideh plate and both were wonderful, juicy and cooked to perfection. The rice was so good, fluffy and well seasoned. We had one plate with the house salad and the other with the cucumber yogurt salad, totally delicious. The bread they serve before your meal arrives is sooo good and it's warm and toasty but soft. It is as if a pita bread and a na'an bread had a baby. REALLY GOOD!
The bathroom was a bit scary (but clean!!) and the whole store very outdated  but the food was so worth it! No pic because I was really just starved to death when I finally got here. I'll be back!
Got the two lobster tails last night for dinner. I thought they weren't the greatest, especially one of them. I woke up this morning with food poisoning. Never going back here again.

Worst Outback I have ever been! After 50 minutes waiting for a steak, I am very surprised to received the steak completely cold, as if was cooked some hours ago.
Then they said to me,sorry!!! 
I am only one ! But I will not be there again ! Ever

Very disappointed.  All tables being used @(no social distancing at all) and a loud obnoxious group took over the bar area and made it their own, with party decor, balloons,etc like they owned the place. And so loud and annoying, honestly so stressful listening to their drunken loud voices and cheering and clapping. I did not enjoy my meal under these stressful conditions.  Worst of all none of these people wore masks!!
So if you want to get Covid, dine here, because they do not care! The day manager, an older man, is not at all nice. He made us wait for an empty table just because he could. And the drinks, just fancy fruit juice, don't waste your money. What a waste of $120.  No more!! This Outback does not care at all about the customer.  That group should have been asked to act more civilized or leave! And masks, please!
Came here for our anniversary last week. Food was delicious and the drinks were fabulous. Alberto is an amazing server and an asset to your restaurant.

Called ahead to make sure the restaurant' was okay with waiting on us 30 minutes before they close...
Replied we serve till 10.
We're seated right away and ordered apps / drinks... took 15 minutes ( it's not busy only 4 tables around us)
The soup is cold, then they bring the wrong soup out...
Now the server acts as if we are bothering her - I asked her if we were bothering her . The response - it's just been a busy day - I care why ? It's called the hospitality business..... so the food is sub par and my Med rare prime rib is rare - not a problem, but no hot au jus .. so 15 minutes later Dustin the manager brings out the au jus ... only because we requested to see a manager..
So while he is at the table - not apologizing, I cut into my prime rib and there is a hair...
So to sum it up, he took my meal off the check - Well ya - I never got to eat it... The food was cold - undercooked - overcooked and was incorrect and we were made to feel like we were bothering them...
I still tipped her 10% and left her a note that she is in the hospitality business...
I rate outback a 3.2 put of 10.....
You might have lost a lifetime customer-the previous visit was also terrible service, but good food....
A Foody

This place is a true hidden gem.  It is hard to find though.  It is located on the lobby floor of the Bankers Life building across from Fairfield Inn and Suites.  Everything is freshly made.  The empanadas are so good, but they sell out fast.  Call ahead if you want some.  

They are open Monday- Friday 7:30 - 3:00.

Great food, both breakfast and lunch menu's!  Recommend their empanada's, either beef or chicken as they are made daily and go quickly!  Located on the ground floor of the building with enough seating and spacing to feel very safe/comfortable.  They also make cafe-con-leche's and Cuban coffee's that are also superb.  Very reasonable priced.  Hot sandwiches made to order.

Great food, both breakfast and lunch menu's!  Recommend their empanada's, either beef or chicken as they are made daily and go quickly!  Located on the ground floor of the building with enough seating and spacing to feel very safe/comfortable.  They also make cafe' con leche's and cuban coffee's that are also superb.  Very reasonable priced.  Hot sandwiches made to order.

Found this place through google and my husband and I were very pleased, and we're very picky when it comes to pizza and wings! I would have personally loved more sauce on my hot wings but maybe next time I can just request more. The pizza was huge and the taste was great! I'd recommend, I'm sure we'll be back!

Not the best. Very overrated from the reviews. I wanted to try this place since I'm literally two stoplights away (I usually get pizza from Anthony's which is very good but I wanted to try something different). I ordered on Saturday evening (2/6/21) a 18" Ham & Pineapple pizza with a side of 10 wings. Wings were good (not as good as BWW though). The pizza was edible but that's it....not much better than a frozen pizza. I rate it under every other place I've had around (Anthony's, Marcos, West Shore, Pizza Hut, papa johns, etc). It's thin crust pizza but the sauce had literally zero flavor...the pizza made me think of eating a piece of cardboard with cheese on it. It was the first time eating from there and more than likely will be the last. Not impressed!
I got the sesame chicken with fried rice and broccoli and I couldn't even eat anymore after two bites. It tasted old and not like chicken at all.

This place deserves all the praises. Their meat is amazing and reasonably priced. I hear the way the halal cows are raised and how the meat is prepared makes for better taste. All I know is I'm always asked to pick up steak from this specific butcher when visiting family.

My husband and I went on a weekend getaway to Tampa from Ft. Lauderdale. We have been wanting to check out Steelbach for brunch for quite some time. We went there for brunch today - and what a disappointment. The hostess & waitress were both unfriendly. We told the waitress it was our first time dining there and she had to response for that. lol we thought she'd make recommendations or let us know what's popular. After taking our orders and giving our food (with a missing item), the waitress never came back to check to see if everything was ok. We had to call her over to tell her the eggs from our order was missing.. so that took another 15 min to come (while the other food that was supposed to be eaten with the eggs got cold). The waitress never apologized for the situation, all she said was they forgot it. She never came back to check in on us throughout our entire meal. We had to call her over again to ask for coffee refill.... and even after requesting it twice, she never refilled the coffee. Anyways, huge disappointment. Would never go back due to service at the location. Management needs to do a better job training their staff.

Would give less than one-star. Had to listen to sirens and make up sex and explicit lyrics while eating a $50 dollar steak. When discussed with the manager they simply dismissed it and said they have no control over the executive music choice. They did acknowledge its not the first-time they have had to discuss this with customers. Needless to say I packed up my family and left. I won't expose them to that nor sponsor and condone that time of customer relations.

Service was excellent. Loved our server Corynne. She had excellent recommendations and knew the menu well. We had the andouille sausage board with pretzel roll, mustard, apple butter and pickled veggies. I hate pickled veggies but otherwise it was good. We each had a cocktail. One was raspberry (mauvelous) and the other was cucumber (Suzy Greenberg). They were very good. My friend had the brick chicken and mac and cheese. Those portions are big. She liked it. I had the grouper. It was very good too. Neither of us are steak eaters so we didn't order it. We know they're known for that. But we figured we'd give it a try! I doubt I'll return though.

I've been wanting to try Steelbach for some time. Located inside Armature Works, I had passed by the front door countless times, until recently, when we stopped in for a birthday celebration in the friend group.

Touting themselves as a Southern inspired kitchen and chop house, Steelbach, partners with local farmers to bring a variety of fresh handpicked flavors to every dish. The portions are hearty, but know that everything in the menu is ala carte.

I ordered the local NY Strip steak cooked medium rare. It was cooked flawlessly, but was unfortunately over seasoned with WAY to much salt, so I had to bury it in the slab of butter that came on the side. Clogged arteries be damned! 

Without doubt, the sides are definitely big enough to share. I split an order of broccoli and an order of Macaroni and Cheese with my wife. Again, the broccoli was WAY over seasoned but the Mac and cheese, which consisted of campanelle pasta, gruyère, lemon, thyme and panko, was totally on point. 

My wife ordered Maud's Fried Chicken and it was enormous! Brined to perfection, the breading was flaky, crisp and light, successfully trapping all of the chickens delicious moisture inside.

One of our friends ordered a weird fruit/bread concoction, but sent it back because the bread was "too dense". The returned product was definitely not the same as the first offering and this time came served already sliced. The fruit did look wonderful though. 

Our service was mostly excellent, however, our waiter hung uncomfortably close and needs to brush his teeth more often. Overall, the experience was quite nice and we would consider going there again if we were in the area.

I've been to Steelbach a few times. While some meals and service have been fantastic, others were lackluster making the place inconsistent. 

Most recently we went for brunch, and despite being one of only a few tables with plenty of waitstaff around, almost all our food came out cold / lukewarm. Our server was also not as attentive as I would expect given the quality of dinner service I've had in the past. 

The monkey bread was delicious, but that's about the only positive I have for brunch. Scored this higher due to past positives with their dinner service.

The food is monstrously fantastic. My wife is pregnant so I ordered take out. I ordered the regular sized pastrami on rye with mustard, regular BLT, 2 orders of the cucumber salad and 2 slices of cake. The regular size for the sandwiches is HUGE and a "slice" of cake weighs more than a sandwich. We're having cake for the next week apparently. This place is great. My only complaint is that they use a little sugar in the cucumber/onion salad. I love it with just vinegar. I can't let it take away from the experience because I should've asked first. Just my preference. Anyway, if you haven't been here yet, it's a traditional Jewish deli that rocks.
This is one of my favorite places to get corned beef sandwiches and hot pastrami sandwiches! I love their food and everyone I ever put on loves it too!

Well it says it in the name folks this place is famous and for a reason!

Think ginormous sandwiches made by quite possibily the best Jewish Delicatessen I have ever come across and I have been eating some dam good Jewish deli meats from when I was a wee lad in grade school.

You really can't go wrong on anything you choose here and they give you a small free chocolate cookie for dessert!

If I lived closer I would probably come here at least once a month but this is the kind of food you have to work out on a weekly if not daily basis to work off the calories you will be endulging on!

If you live in Philadelphia and have not been here shame on you, get here ASAP!!

As always people SYOY!!!

Food: 4.25 Out of 5
My goodness the portions at this place weren't what I expected. I ordered one of their specialty sandwiches, someone with corn beef & pastrami because those are my favorite cuts. Also ordered a slice of the cannoli cake. Flavors delivered and the portions justified the price.

Service: 4.5 out 5
Friendly folks working the counter. We ordered to go, but still had an enjoyable experience.

Environment: 4 Out of 5
A lot of open seating, but we didn't feel comfortable dining indoors, no physical barrier separating clientsThankfully there are benches & tables across the way from the restaurant. 

Overall:4.25 Out of 5
Taking my out of the area friends and family to try this neighborhood joint!

It was great to see that the bakery and deli of famous fourth Street is in full swing in 2021. We just stopped by to pick up some takeout and were thrilled that we could get everything on the menu thank you

My wife and I went on a Friday night and hung out til about midnight and we had a great time. The dancers were really nice (and gorgeous) and not pushy (Stevie especially was fantastic, she gave us a couples dance and hung out with us for a bit). The bartenders/waitresses/masseuse were all attentive without being pushy. There were a couple dozen dancers around by the end of the night, but (and this is my only complaint) towards 11PM it was a little hard to get their attention for dances. We wanted to get a few more dances but it just wasn't in the cards. We'll be going back soon though, it quickly became my wife's favorite bar!

If you're looking for a good club to visit as a couple, I'd highly recommend this one, but maybe go a tad earlier so your night doesn't peter out like ours did. We'll try happy hour next time. That said, everyone was polite, it was clean, no one was weird, and it was an incredibly entertaining evening.

This team needs serious training from a managers perspective. Worst customer service and over staffed. They are not team players. And some workers just stand or talk inappropriately in front of customers. I can see this going out of business in the future because of the work flow and customer service. No napkins provider or utensils. Threw my fried in a bag unwrapped. Unsanitary.

Five stars all around. Live band. Quality gin. Good food. Great service.

Came by with a reservation for 7 or so for a Friday night and were seated quickly! Everyone is really kind and on top of it - opening doors, communicating with each other and whatnot. Good team, it seemed.

We had an extremely accommodating waiter who was just so on top of it - clearing plates, getting extra rounds for drinks, explaining the gin.

The octopus was prepared very well and had amazing flavor! I would definitely get it again.

I also went to town on the endive salad. Super refreshing.

The singers were talented and their voices fueled my soul!
First stop during our walk around Savannah downtown. Love that the area is open container and we can enjoy the outdoors while sipping on refreshing cocktails or libation of choice.

We came across this bar on our last day in Tampa. We decided to rent a bird scooter -which was a ton of fun- and sight see, when I saw this big, beautiful lit up sign that said Gin Joint. It literally made me stop in my tracks, being that Gin is pretty much the only type of alcohol I drink, and decide to pop in. 

When you go in through the first set of doors you are greeted by two hostesses and a doorman. They were incredibly warm and friendly. They gave us some information about the place and allowed us to take a peek inside. It was beautiful, the light was dimmed just perfectly, beautiful suede couches to eat at, regular tables as well, nice art and lighting and a gorgeous, long bar with so many different varieties of Gin. They do have other types of alcohol as well but if you're going somewhere called the Gin Joint, you should definitely try a gin drink. 

If nothing on the cocktail menu screams to you, ask the bartender to make you something along the flavor profiles you do like. They are REAL bartenders. He was amazing! I tried a cocktail on the menu that had cucumber and lemon and it was incredibly refreshing. However, I gave the bartender free reign on my next drink and it was, by far, my favorite gin drink EVER -and I've had a lot of gin drinks lol.

The staff was extremely warm and attentive. The bartender was pretty funny and I loved his candor. The bar was completely full and we were lucky enough to have a wonderful couple next to us that we spoke to the entire time. Oh! And one of the best parts was that they had live music. They had a soulful band playing and singing live. It was music we all new but more of an RnB/ballads playlist, perfect for the ambiance. 

Unfortunately, we didn't get to try the food because we had just previously eaten a big meal but I WILL be back because it looked and smelled amazing. All in all, the staff was attentive and warm. The drinks were amazing, as was the vibe. I definitely recommend adding this as a must visit while in Downtown Tampa but if you can MAKE RESERVATIONS. The hostess did tell us the actual tables do book up way in advance. The bar, however, is first come first serve.
Had a Spectacular evening last night!  Our waiter, Ki, the food, the entertainment & manager Brent all exceeded our expectations. This is an absolute must dining experience in Tampa.

I have to say this place is spectacular.  Make a reservation.  The evening started with top notch host staff.  We did not have a reservation another party of 2 canceled and they were able to accommodate us.  The evening continued to get better from there our server was amazing and food delicious.  The Live music and decor went together perfect.  When in Tampa again we definitely will be back.
Great atmosphere and good beer selection. Staff is friendly and the weather was amazing!
The Founding Fathers would definitely approve. High praise for this little slice of paradise. Brady and Elise kept us entertained with impeccable service and good fun. Go and have fun!
The Founding Fathers would definitely approve. High praise for this little slice of paradise. Brady and Elise kept us entertained with impeccable service and good fun.

Honestly such an amazing place! In the center of downtown and has a true Philly charm! Right next to independence Hall and the Liberty Bell! Great place to stop by while site seeing! Elise is amazing!!

This is an amazing place to hang out with your mates for just a nice kick back night or if you want to go hard. But this is all thanks to their star super employee Elise. She is hands down the kindest and just most amazing person in the world. Thank you for the good times Elise.

If the word "disappointment" had a physical manifestation, it would be the Tampa Bay Airport Panda Express. Not only was the food sub-par for a Panda Express, which I recognize as not authentic already as it is, but it came in very disappointing proportions, they were cooking a fresh pot of chow-mein as I ordered and instead of waiting 30 seconds, or even dishing my meat up first, the server took a spoon out from under the counter to scrape the scraps out of the bowl, into my tray. Then to proceed by closing it and I essentially ended up with 1/3 of the chow-mein you would normally expect. Plus to top it off it was the trash off the bottom that you couldn't even eat with chopsticks. The orange chicken and Beijing beef were a little soggy. But lacked a lot of the flavor that other Panda locations provide. Overall extremely disappointing experience today. Unacceptable. Is the only word I can think of to use to review this branch of a normally decent franchise.

Amazing experience out in the patio covered space during a white out storm over looking Channelside.

Sit in the couch space by the wall just the two of you, it's refreshing. 
Food was delicious and drinks were so creative.

I paired the vegetable croquettes with the french fries.
& as for drinks my favorite was Lavender Fields.

Valet is an option but they don't validate. So the best option is around the corner in a $2/hr city garage.

Amazing experience out in the patio covered space during a white out storm over looking channelside.

Sit in the couch space by the wall just the two of you, it's refreshing without getting drenched.


Food was delicious and drinks were so creative and delicious. Great experience!
Park in the City garage for $2 n hr or you can do valet.

The potential for SIX palpable but the execution is lacking from top to bottom. For the price points you expect solid service and a somewhat upscale dining experience but in reality SIX is an overpriced poolside restaurant. For context, we were a table of 5 with the dining room at ~25% capacity. It took a solid hour+ from putting in orders for drinks and apps to actually receiving them (both) which was the first red flag. Then when they did arrive everything was incredibly underwhelming. The shrimp ceviche is clearly previously frozen, potentially previously cooked shrimp in some sauce. The chicken meatball was pretty good and the same goes for the crudo. The drinks were outrageously priced given the quality and actual quantity in each glass. Not relevant to the review but the waiter provided a kids menu along with regular menus for what was clearly a business dinner. 

Given that we were over 1.5 hours in, at this point we decided to audible somewhere else for dinner. When you sit down and look around you can't help but feel like you are in a fancy cafeteria from the tables, to the lighting in the room, to people walking through in bathing suits w/ towels. 

Hoping they are working through some of the kinks that come with opening a new restaurant but had high hopes given the reputation of JW's. For the price point there are numerous better options around Tampa.

Horrible food and slow service. My sister and I went there for lunch, we chose to sit at a high table by the bar since the dining room was empty. I have ordered a burger, it took nearly 40 min to get our food. The wait was ridiculously long for a burger and an appetizer plus the stools were  so uncomfortable.  The burger was medium rare instead of medium well, the bottom bun was soggy and drenched in oil. Let's not forget about the horrendous cheese which I had to scrape. I hate to write a negative review but charging $19 for a tasteless burger is outrageous.

Pretty average . Not too many options near the Marriott.  The rib eye was good but it was cut in half , not sure if the chef knew how to cook the steak correctly.. they say thats how they present their steaks . The clam chowder was pretty salty also

Enjoyed bowling on Father's Day with Hubby & Kids. Nice atmosphere, very clean. 2 Down faults, the women & men restrooms are located in the same enterance area. The bartender/food order taker, didn't wear gloves when she touched the fruit as she made drinks. She collected money/credit cards, punched the orders in on the computer and grabbed the fruit with the same hand. She was awesome though, she did it all. I left this message for the manager.

Came here to bowl, play shuffleboard, bocce, pool...
PROS:
Atmosphere 
Food 

CONS:
 Rude employees (manager, bouncer, shoe people)
Pins don't set correctly (bowling at 7 pins)
Drinks $$$ and mostly ice 

I won't come back, the people  running this place don't care about customer service, they made one our little kids move to different seating and yelled at them when using the ATM to play the broken hockey game
I just started coming to this deli and I love It! Didn't realize the hours changed and came in right after closing and they still got my order. Super nice! And Great food! Wish I found this sooner!

You know I've always loved the devil crabs and cuban sandwiches at Michelle's. Now I cant stop thinking about the lemon cake! I remember when she first started the business and was located on 15th street in East Tampa when I was a little girl. I was delighted to hear of her location that opened on Ray Charles Blvd, that is now closed. The current location is closer to the Clerk of Circuit Courthouse in downtown Tampa and provides minimal and frustrating parking as most downtown locations. One thing that has not changed over the years is the extensive wait time to receive your order. It does not matter if you call ahead, do expect to wait an additional 15-30 minutes to receive your sandwich. I'm not sure how to get around this unless you call in and wait another 45 minutes before picking up your order, in efforts to minimize the wait and save on time. The sandwiches are crafted by Michelle and draw a consistent crowd, the new location is bright, spacious and roomy for groups, but the never ending wait times are just a turn off for me.
The Cuban bread is seasoned  sooo much flavor in this Lois & Clark sandwich.. the restaurant is big, clean & the service is great. I highly recommend!

I only give a 3 because of location and hours of business. As if finding parking to go here isn't bad enough, your ONLY open through the week?!? Why not Saturday, AT LEAST?! I love the food but 'once in a while when I just so happen to be off through the week and actually think of it' is not enough. Do better guys. Did I mention the food is great, btw?!

The drive-thru line is always SUPER long no matter what day or time of day. The time that I went, I walked in the store to order inside instead, and they were only allowing mobile app orders, but no one was allowed to walk in and order there. Despite this, the drive thru line was still super slow and took almost 40 minutes to get to the window. The food is usually fine here, but it is pretty disorganized and really slow for fast food.

This is the worst chick-fil-a I have ever been to. First off, there's only one line for the drive through. Second, the wait took for ever to go through it. And lastly, this was the first time I ever got a chick-fil-a sandwich where it was warm instead of hot. How disappointing.

We just ate at Asian Wok for the first time and really enjoyed our meal. The food was fresh. I ordered Mongolian beef and, since I don't really like spicy food, asked for it to be made not so spicy. My meal was perfect. My husband ordered a beef dish with scallops and he enjoyed his meal as well. The restaurant seemed to be very clean and the staff members wore masks while we were present. The restaurant appears to be family owned with all the family members helping. They provided great service! We will visit again! Thanks for a wonderful dinner.

ANOTHER FIND!!! When it comes to take out food I'll prob always post the left overs because I want to enjoy my food hot. LOL But Asian Wok is delicious!! We ordered the Sweet and sour chicken, beef broccoli, pork fried rice, and the hunan beef ( spicy) sooo good! The pork fried rice had good bite size pork pieces very tasty 
The sweet and sour had the perfect breading and the chicken taste so good. When I picked up my order I was greeted by a little girl she is such a doll and sooooo cute! Definitely will be back to try the lo Mein and chow mein. The egg rolls are amazing too and super big!  The food didn't leave us feeling bloated which I loved! Very tasty food! Highly recommend.

Called to make sure they use 00" flour to make their pizzas and they said yes. Asked for a marghertia and they made it. Hands down the best pizza in the area, so glad I tried them. Owner and the girl there were both very sweet. Def coming back!

I want to update my review because a lot has happened in the last year. As I mentioned previously, my first visit to Pizzeataly was early on in the pandemic. A couple of subsequent pizzas last summer were of the same excellent quality & equally delicious. But unfortunately, in November of 2020, their food truck was stolen! Yes, STOLEN! I never heard if the thieves were caught and/or if their food truck was recovered, but Pizzeataly was able to reopen in late January. I was delighted to again be able to enjoy that wood-fired oven-baked pizza in a personal pie size, with my favorite toppings of spinach, chicken and feta & mozzarella cheeses. Then, a few weeks ago, Pizzeataly relocated about a mile away, on the east side of Hanley Rd just north of Hillsborough Ave. Here, they have several tables for outdoor dining, including a few with umbrellas. So now they're even closer to my house!

Five star service and food. Called them at 4:30 for a 6:45 pickup with an order for three pizzas.  I got there at 6:35 and they were just boxing them up for me while I paid.   Very good pizza, all my friends liked it a lot - so much better than the chain places.  This is now my go-to pizza joint.

Owner is super friendly over the phone and in person, took my order and nailed it perfectly, I wish him much success.
First time ordering from Pizzeataly and I was so happy ! The pizza was amazing and the lasagna was delicious. Not overly salty or overly seasoned. I will definitely be ordering again!!!

This is easily the best pizza in Tampa. The pizza crust is flavorful and baked just right without being burnt.  They place a generous amount of toppings on the pizzas too.  In my opinion Pizzeataly is an excellent value- large pizzas of excellent quality at a good price. I highly recommend them.

North Philly Chinese To-Go level food at high end Chinatown prices. $12.95 for broccoli and chicken? $3.50 fpor a small Wonton? My bill was$19 bucks! That's a 6.95 lunch special or $9.95 dinner at best for the food I received.
The food is fine, average Chinatown level but I think the price is above Chinatown average since the portion seems small compared to other Chinatown restaurants.

So I ordered delivery food from this restaurant and I found a super moldy cauliflower in my food. So I contact the restaurant and ask for a refund just for this single dish I ordered. The other 3 dishes aren't very tasty either, but they are just simply not as tasty and nothing else goes wrong. Guess what they told me "we throw all our unhealthy ingredients, please PICK OUT the ingredients that seems not fresh and CONTINUE EATING" 

I don't know they said that to me because I ordered through delivery and can't give the rest of food back to them or they genuinely think cooked MOLD is edible. The delivery company felt super bad and refund me credits, but I feel bad for them because it's not even their responsibilities. 

Guys, open your eyes and run away from them, there are so many good Chinese restaurant around that provides better food and customer service. While this place needs a visit from the health department.

This is  the worst pizza hut I've ever dealt with. I would give 000 stars, Very UNHAPPY with pizza hut. I placed an order online,  to be delivered at 7pm, the order was completed around 5:45pm 05/18/2021.  7:30pm comes and goes. I call and ask what happened to my order,  the young lady that answered the phone said, the  order was cancelled, because no drivers to deliver, I said and you didn't think to call me, then I spoke to the manager the next morning, and he said they tried to call, but there was no record of them calling on my phone, his excuse was drivers are hard to find mentiroso, this manager is a SAD excuse for a manager.   I then called West Shore Pizza,  placed the identical order, it was at the house in 45 minutes, and $15.00 dollars cheaper, obviously they were able to find drivers. Will never be calling pizza hut again, they SUCK

Great place to order from if you want an hour to go by , not have food, be on hold 40 minutes until they close, spend $55 and then have no dinner because everything else is now closed too. 2nd time it's happened

This place is literally the worst place to get pizza in Florida. It's seems almost like you landed smack dab in a Seinfeld episode. All three employees sitting around doing nothing and have attitudes. Pizza was old and the place was disgustingly filthy. They rarely  wipe down tables, clean bathrooms or sweep the floor. The city should look into this business before someone gets sick. Please close your doors. The people that walk through the door can tell you hate your life and business by the effort you put forth in your customer service and food. Let a real business owner offer a better product to the community.
Horrible. Had to stop at airport on layover. Grabbed a Turkey burger and sweet potato fries. The burger taste like it was marinated in SALT. The fries tasted old.

This random listing came up on my Uber eats with a buy 1 get 1 burrito deal.  Not knowing what this was I wanted to dig in and try this deal. So ordered the fries burrito with chicken and one with beef.  

Searching for this spot I had no idea where/what this was until I had to call Uber eats and they told me check behind the library.  I thought it might have been a ghost kitchen inside the Acme but not so. 

Politely surprised at the massive size of the burritos.  They were also tasty better than Chipotle which I think are bland and flavorless and these come with a side of cheese sauce if you ask.  Overall awesome bogo deal.  It was originally listed at $14 but now comes in at $16.  I would never buy one at that price but with the deal makes it worth it.

Uhhh yes please! Long wait but worth it. We were looking for some new stuff around the area and found this hidden gem. Best Mexican-infused food I've ever had in Philly. I hope this pop up never goes away! That fried cheesecake was super bomb! Or should I say hella bomb ;)

Just ordered off GrubHub however the driver couldn't find the location. I really wanted to give this place a shot so I went out myself and found it easily, so any food delivery driver's reading this you have no excuses. Anyways, I'm really glad I did go out and pick this up myself. Food is incredible! Anything less than 4 stars is unreasonable. The two gentlemen working the kitchen were personable and professional. This will likely be one of my new "go to" spots.

This is a ghost kitchen located in a trailer behind Saladworks. They do not list a phone number and there are no directions anywhere so it was pretty hard to find...

They have a lot of interesting menu items that sound amazing on paper but the execution just isn't there. The meat is dry, the queso tastes really funky, the burritos fall apart and you just expect a lot more overall. Even with things like Flamin Hot Cheetos and Doritos added, the dishes still taste so bland... The only main dish I liked was the Flamin Cali Crunch which is their take on a crunchwrap supreme. Honestly their best items are the deserts like the deep fried Oreos and cookie dough, but that's hard to mess up...

This place is so awesome, food is excellent, staff is so friendly and warm, just like being with family!!! Excellent service, excellent people and excellent food!!! I'd recommend this place to anyone!!!!
Love their meatballs and gravy  - best I have had ina long time. Super friendly and accommodating staffing

Great little spot in Tacony. Went with 6 people and sat comfortably in their little Italian shop. The pasta was fresh and the Gravy was great! I had Veal Parmigiana, was a great cut . The prices are  low too, the waitress was personable and the chefs(owners) came to our table to ask how things were. We will be back for sure!

I'm somewhat stunned by these reviews. I've lived in Philly for a number of years, have been to Angelo's and C+S, and while this place might not be a destination, it's pretty great for a neighborhood spot! The guy is nice and the dough is awesome. I like the tomato and ricotta slice.

Owner thought it was appropriate to aggressively scream at and threaten me at 9 pm when he was driving down a one way street the incorrect way, in response to zero hostility on my end and me reversing my car out of the alley so he could continue to drive the down the street the wrong way. I am young and a woman- I was scared and felt unsafe- he intended to scare me. We used to occasionally come here- on top of the rude and disrespectful owner, this is horrible pizza that clearly sits out for a very long time. Please do not support this business. Rione Pizza is down just one more block at 21st and Samsom, go there instead for better food and atmosphere.

Owner thought it was appropriate to scream at and threaten me at 9 pm when he was driving down a one way street the incorrect way. Also, we used to occasionally come here- on top of the clearly rude and disrespectful owner, this is horrible pizza that clearly sits out for a very long time.
The Apple Dumpling with Heavy Cream is everything and more for living your best life!  What a treat! Definitely worth the hype.
Visited on a Saturday morning around 10am and got seats at the counter right away. Food was served within about 10 minutes of ordering. It was hot and delicious. Service was friendly!

Visited here on a Friday morning and the counter was packed. We took a seat and we're quickly served upon. I think our server's name was Ellie. She was quick (and busy) and there were no issues with our order. The food was okay-- French toast was really good but the veggie omelette had something left to be desired. The tomatoes were still green and the green peppers were over cooked. All veggies were too big, so dicing would've been nice.
An excellent choice for an informal breakfast. My pot roast sandwich is worth a repeat. Good omelettes too.

Cyndy's Bottom Line:  Great spot for a hearty yummy breakfast & coffee.

*Located in Reading Terminal
*Check in for a counter seat
*Nice friendly & efficient service
*Vast selection of breakfast items.
*Smooth, delicious coffee
*Known for the apple dumplings

This is what we ate:
*Breakfast BLT - a BLT with your choice of bread.  Topped off with a perfectly cooked egg with crispy bacon just the right amount of mayo with a tomato slice and lettuce.  Built nice and neatly to eat.  Yummy!

*Blueberry pancakes with crispy bacon - pancake sprinkled with sweet blueberries.  Good yummy texture.  Bacon nice and crispy.

I will return here for the apple dumpling!
Highly recommend.

I took my partner to Gabriella's on Tuesday night to celebrate a birthday. I originally made a reservation for outdoor dining but was given a table indoor. I asked the hostess why it was changed and wasn't given a clear indication why. Server took awhile to acknowledge us for our order. Appetizer came out and it was very good. Mains came out without the sides. Server NEVER came back to check on us regarding the sides, ask us if everything was ok, or to fill our water glasses. Eventually one of the sides came out after we had eaten half our entrees, but the other side (brussel sprouts) never came out. If the quality of the service matched the quality of the food, I would definitely come back again. MAD AS HELL.

We were so excited to try this! It took a while to get a reservation but the day finally came! Our reservation was for 7:45 pm. We arrived a little early (7:41) and were told our table was not yet ready. We waited about 10 minutes and were seated. The prices are not included on the online menu and I know why: the prices were about 40% above where they should have been! We placed our order and sat, and sat, and sat.......it was about almost over an hour later when we finally got our meal. Was it worth the wait....heck NO! The food came out luke warm. The flavors were nothing spectacular (at least not worth the $34 I spent on the prawn dish). I get better more flavorful Vietnamese food at my local small hole in the wall Vietnamese restaurant (at a fraction of the cost). I really feel like I got robbed out of at least the $50 or so dollars I overspent at this restaurant. DO NOT waste your time or money! Go to that local hole in the wall restaurant, you will thank me!

Hit this place up! My mind was blown. 

My friend and I had made a reservation when we first heard about it, and the potential rain quashed our outside dinning reservations and we called and they fit us inside. That was super awesome of them. 

This place is BYO which is clutch. We enjoyed the chicken dumplings which were a good dumpling; not revolutionary but really good. We LOVED the tamales and the savory crepes. I will return and I will order these again. The shaking beef was awesome and so was the salted egg fried rice. The brussel sprouts were super solid. I would recommend anything on the menu. It doesn't seem like you can order a mediocre thing. 

The wait staff was excellent, and super attentive. I love that you can see into the kitchen.

Authentic Vietnamese flavors and unique dishes you can't get anywhere else. I love that Gabriella's is opening up peoples idea of what true Vietnamese food really is. Every dish is a must try, you won't be disappointed!

tl;dr a chic Vietnamese BYOB offering a sophisticated take on street food

I always appreciate the eclectic and innovative dining experiences that define East Passyunk. A newcomer to the neighborhood and taking up residence in the space formerly operated by Sate Kampar, Gabriella's Vietnam certainly has big shoes to fill. The deep room sports a sleek bar top in the middle and the kitchen in the back. The purposefully chipped plaster walls expose the brick underneath. Planters and incandescent bulbs hang from the black ceilings, setting a paradoxically sophisticated yet cozy mood. Minimalistic wooden furniture matched the worn hardwood floors, and each table was furnished with faux China plates and plastic chopsticks.

My partner and I, armed with a bottle of red, stopped by early for the weekend dinner service. We opted for the Bánh Bèo Chén (water fern dumplings), Bò Lúc Lắc (shaken beef), and Cua Lột Rang Trứng Muối (soft-shell crabs). The dumpling platter was a sight to behold, with many individual dumpling dishes served on a woven bamboo basket. The flavors represented a unique balance of rich (similar to egg yolk), chalky, and sour (from the vinegar source). However, I was disappointed that the fried pork skin ended up chewy and tough rather than crispy. Also, eating the dumplings was challenging, with each dish representing closer to a bite and a half and single-bite, and the rice cake readily fell apart before I could ever get it to my mouth. While interesting, I probably would not order this again. The crab was heavily seasoned with salt, pepper, and garlic, then fried and served halved. As a big fan of soft-shelled crab, I was in heaven. My only critique was that I would have liked it fried slightly crispier. Meanwhile, the shaken beef had the spice profile of beef jerky (which I wholeheartedly intend as a compliment) mixed with premium, tender meat. I was particularly impressed by the piquant lime sauce.

At the conclusion of our meal, we were left satisfied but not wholely full -- I'd say one additional dish would have been appropriate for a hungry party of two. While Gabriella's was nearly empty when we arrived, it was fully buzzing at our departure. With food cooked-to-order, expect to wait accordingly. Service was attentive, but borderline robotic. The $80 (after tax and tip) for our meal felt somewhat expensive. While our appetizer left something to be desired, the mains stood out well enough to me to crave a visit back.
Unfortunately, I did not want my pudding with mold. Very disappointed. I used to other from here a lot, but this is unacceptable

If you're looking for an authentic Cuban sandwich shop in Tampa, this is your place. I can usually judge a sandwich shop by the quality of the bread. 

Aguila's is authentic Cuban bread/baguette with the right amount of chew and crunch. I love to order the Medianoche (Midnight sandwich) and fresh fries, which is a twist on a traditional Cuban sandwich involving a layer of mojo infused pulled pork. It's tender, delicious, not overly wet or dry, just perfect. 

The owner/manager is very friendly and happy to talk to a fresh face. We don't get to frequent Aguilas that often, but seeing how the owner interacts with his regulars, there are quite a few people that make the restaurant a very frequent stop.

So, first and foremost, this is a sandwich shop. Small tables and a small dining room with simple decor is what to expect and appreciate about Aguilas. It's not fine dining. It's not haute cuisine. It's not dressy nor is it stuffy. It's a relaxed place where the Tampa local community gathers together for lunch over a quality sandwich and a cup of espresso at a reasonable price.

If you're down with that, you'll love it. It's not earth shattering and mind warping food. It's fresh, solid, well executed and superbly made sandwiches that you'll grow to crave.
Went down in vacation and tried some Cuban Sandwiches, my taste buds loved this shops. To be honest I didn't find a bad one but this one was my personal favorite

While I do believe back in the day it was better; it's still not even close to a bad sandwich. One of the best traditional Cubans and a media Noches in Tampa.  Still one of my favorite Cuban sandwich shops after possibly 10 years.

This place is one of those Tampa institutions that have been around for forever. While I wish indoor dining was allowed, with the pandemic still ongoing, I was ok with sitting outside. Went with a friend in the late afternoon and service was slow. People here were definitely taking their time making the sandwiches. Good thing I wasn't in a rush that day! However, the Cuban sandwich was indeed delicious. For a regular sized Cuban, the sandwich was massive. It was probably close to a foot long. Can't imagine how big a large would be in that case. I love that the bread is nice and crusty on the outside yet soft and warm on the inside. The ham, cheese, pork, and lettuce totally work in harmony. Favorite part was the pork. Nice and moist, it provides so much savory flavor that gets soaked into the bread. In short, service can be hit or miss. But the Cuban is solid here and if you have time to kill, it's a good place to chill and get some solid food :)

I ordered delivery from this place and by reading all the reviews, I was really excited. The food is EXTREMELY salty and the spices are overtaking the flavor of the chicken. I've never had a curry that bad! I'm not sure how this is considered to be "gourmet"
Every thing was great.I come here every couple months but when I do I'm satisfied..thank u

Overcooked shrimp and mussels. What they call curry was unrecognizable by ANY standard - underseasoned and watery. Dry rice - it tasted stale.  Indifferent staff could not be bothered with any questions.  Never going back

This spot is the best! Came here from New York and I want to come back and try EVERYTHING on the menu. Stand outs were the Caribbean curry fries like OH MY GOODNESS it was sooo good. And the portions here? I came home with enough to eat in front of my television and I'm honestly looking forward to it. chef Johnson personally came out after which really touched us because that food has LOVE and EFFORT in it! Appetizer set the tone and dessert some strawberry ice box cake just ended it nicely. Thank you Diana and Marie for the service also it was OUTSTANDING!

I love this little cafe - we have eaten here a few times and they always have a great selection of fresh pastries as well as cool merchandise and large selection of fresh deli meat.

I though it was kind of strange to have a coffee shop and deli combo but Bower Cafe makes it work. This time I got avocado toast with bacon. It had too much avocado for liking and the bacon was not well-done but that's on me for not asking. I really enjoyed it despite not meeting my usual specifications.

The coffee drinks are great and I will be back soon to see what they have in store!
Good cold brew. The Bev was delicious. Fresh avocado and warm mozzarella with just the right spice from the radishes. Lots of options for meat-free. Friendly staff. Nice atmosphere. Will be back!

Went here with a friend for breakfast and it was so tasty and such a nice vibe that we stayed for lunch and got some nice open face toast sandwiches. Loved the cured meats, many options but unfortunately not all are available all the time. They were very kind and gave us a sample to taste before we ordered. The toast came out delicious and beautifully presented as well, for an affordable price :)

Small, very quaint shop with a hidden patio out back.  Serves La Colombe, pastries and charcuterie.  The guy (owner) behind the counter makes it even better, a warm, gracious and welcoming host.  Thumbs up!
Super cute cafe with really great service. They also have delicious pastries! I will certainly be back to try more baked goods in the future!
Nice Hookah Bar, with outside seating and an excellent bar and wait staff. Pretty good food and excellent drink, Burt is an amazing bar tender.

This place is great. I used to go there every Thursday. They have great sangrias options. As well, the best thing is that they have a dogs' menu. This place is located close by to the dog park where I used to take my dog. After the dog park, it was cool to go and grab some sangria. I had sangria and my dog meanwhile enjoyed the peanut butter flatbread. Honestly, the flatbread looked so good that I would eat it by myself.
Sangria is nasty don't waste your time if you're coming for it. Other than that large portions nice venue good hookah spot

This place is terrible...DONT WASTE YOUR TIME...I came here with some friends got there around 11pm and shortly after was showen to a table. It was all down hill after that. We waited 20mins for someone to order a hookah with then another 30 for someone to actually bring it. This whole time we are also waiting for the bartender; who's moving at snail speed. Once we finally got our drinks (around midnight!!!) I asked the bartender what time they closed. He responded "now". Security and Ruby ("the manager") quickly began to kick people out. Ruby  explained to me that he had been ticketed and I was being problematic by requesting to be able to finish my drinks and hookah that i had just revived before having to leave. He continued to explain his $1200 ticket and how nice he was for being  able to give us a table. Him being ticketed is not my concern as a customer and his staff's lack of hospitality and efficiency quickly cancelled out the fact that we had chairs in a HALF EMPTY CLUB..everyone had a table!!! He then offered us a free hookah for next time. I gladly told him me nor any of my friends would be returning and asked for a refund for the hookah, which was denied.

Nice atmosphere , service is pretty good, however when it comes to menu items, a description would be helpful.
I ordered the rock star chicken tacos and didn't find out that they were spicy until the first bite.

The owner had an attitude after I mentioned I'm not allowed to have anything Spicy and that a detailed description in regards to food item would be helpful for future references 

First time here and probably the last!!!!!
You can't have an attitude in regards to an item description not being accurate .

We stumbled upon this new little pizzeria in the Italian Market. It's in a small corner storefront next to the parking lot/eating area on 9th St by Washington. Very convenient to grab a slice and sit to eat it. After eating lunch and walking through Passyunk Ave and the market, we were looking for a little something to eat. A piece of pizza was perfect!
You order your pizza at the window. The staff were friendly. It was a little annoying that the prices listed were for plain pizza which wasn't available. The margarita we ordered a dollar more per slice at $3.50. 
The pizza was Square with a nice amount of sauce and cheese. The sauce had a touch of sweetness. The crust had some crunch but was a little soggy in the bottom. 
I would probably grab a slice here again if they had the regular . With so many places to eat pizza in South Philly prices here are a little high.
Amazing pizza, great people! Reminds me of Joe's pizza in NYC. I always want to stop by here for a slice or more!
We got the Buffalo chicken pizza and the pepperoni garlic knots- absolutely bangerang.

If you like thin crust and crunchy texture, you're gonna love their Tomato Pie (square)! I've been on the lookout for good closeby pizza places ever since Lorenzos Pizza sort of lost their "taste"  I'm glad that I can now rely on Nannie Franco's for my pizza cravings! As for their pepperoni slice, it is quite oily, but the taste is pretty good as well. Same for the white slice! 

Other things to note: They take cash and Venmo. There's a nice, christmas-lighted(?) open area next to it with a bunch of tables and chairs if you wanted to sit down and eat.

It took me such a long time to try here but now I am obsessed. So far I've tried their buffalo chicken pizza -- the chicken is grilled & tastes fresh, and there is the perfect balance of buffalo sauce with blue cheese. I'm admittedly not a fan of blue cheese but their sauce isn't overpowering so it works well! 

Their regular plain pizza is also a hit. Their crust is nice and thin while also having the perfect amount of flake. 

The real hit though (for me) is their white pizza. It was AMAZING and had such a great garlic flavor. I enjoyed every bite of it!

tl;dr a Korean spin on American bar fare, falling more heavily on the latter cuisine

Promising Korean fusion eats just out of Rittenhouse, Southgate is a popular neighborhood gastropub. I've walked by it countless times, but only just made the time to give it a whirl. The gray-toned palette skips between matte and glossy finishes to compliment dim mood lighting. The walls are decked with a chic take on subway tile. Exposed HVAC, incandescent bumps, and twinkle lights dangle tastefully from the ceiling. Hours and specials are chalked onto a board at the head of the sleek bar that extends the length of the restaurant.

My partner and I swung by for early weekend dinner and arrived in time for happy hour. We opted for the Banchan Set, the Bulgogi and Pork Steamed Buns, the Korean Fried Chicken, and the Bulgogi Burger (which came with a draft, as part of HH). Of the banchan, my favorites were the zucchini and tofu, both cooked in a rich soy-based sauce and served hot. On the other hand, the kimchi and cucumbers were lukewarm and standard, if not boring. Each dish was large, and I recognize that Southgate is not an authentic Korean restaurant; yet, it still felt off-script for Southgate to charge for banchan. The two-biter buns both had a pillowy bun and nice spicy mayo. While spicy pork was flavorful (and particularly heavy on the sesame), the bulgogi felt dry. Both KFC glazes were yummy with a remarkable depth of flavor (even though the "spicy" was not particularly hot). However, they ran a tad soggy with a laughable tiny portion (7 small wings) for the price. The burger was rich, juicy, thick, and heavy, complemented nicely by the tang of pickles and subtly spicy aioli. but was paired with a flimsy bun and flimsier steakhouse fries (I really wish they were shoestring, instead).

At $56 (after tax and tip) despite the happy hour deals, Southgate definitely errs on the expensive end. Although nothing was actively negative about my experience here, nothing floored me either. As a whole, Southgate definitely rings more American food than Korean -- so if you have a hankering for Korean comfort food, this probably won't do the trick. I may or may not even return to Southgate, depending on whether I ever have the craving for their specific take on fusion cuisine.

This place had been on my list for YEARS, probably since it opened.  Finally got around to ordering from there a while back and it was worth the hype.

Ordered some bao buns, spicy pork miso ramen, beef bibimbap and Korean fried chicken.  All of it was fantastic, layered with flavor and you get a lot of bang for your buck, but THAT FRIED CHICKEN THO.  Let's just say I'll never eat regular basic bitch fried chicken again in my life.  Southgate has officially converted me.  How does it get so crispy? So juicy? So succulent? So sweet and tangy? It's dark magic, indeed.

I did enjoy the other dishes, but honestly everything paled in comparison to the chicken.  I would just stick to that, honestly (although their burger sounded enticing).

Yummm! I made reservations for me and my friends for dinner Friday night. Right now they are doing outdoor dining only which is fine! They had a cute little outdoor set up. We were promptly seated and ordered our food since we were starving.
It was the tail end of happy hour so I also ordered the soju punch before it ended. I didn't care for the drink I got but drank it since it was only 8$. For food I started with the soy fried chicken appetizer. Then for my entree I got the bulgogi burger with fries.
The appetizer came out and omg there was so much chicken. It was all crispy and juicy! The sauce was really good too :) My bulgogi burger came out and it was pretty messy to eat but had a good bulgogi burger. It was slightly overcooked but other than that it was still really good. They give you a mountain of fries with the burger which is great! My friends got the tofu bibimbaps (vegan and vegetarian friendly!) And my other friend got the spice pork baos and the seoul hot chicken sandwich. Everyone enjoyed their meals and we were happily full. I had tons of leftovers after  :) great place! Can't wait to come back and try more items.

Ok so if you are ordering the Korean fries, you probably cannot eat anything else - the portion size is humongous! I had the bibimbap and the boyfriend had a burger - both were delicious! Staff was super friendly and attentive. They also have a great cocktail menu so definitely keeping this on my "go back" list.

Southgate is one of our favorite neighborhood spots. Outdoor tables are 6+ feet apart, covered, and heated for up to 4 guests. Try the bibimbap bowl with tofu for a hearty vegetarian meal!

In an effort to call attention to COVID-safe outdoor dining done well and support local businesses, I have started an Instagram account @PhillyCovidDiningGuide showing the outdoor setups at restaurants! Check out my post on Southgate and others here https://www.instagram.com/phillycoviddiningguide/
It's amazing place with best coffee and friendly staff. Thanks so much. Your coffee do my day best!

Always come here for the iced Caramel delight. Got larges today and a little disappointed that they just taste like milk. I'll stick with the regular size next time unless I feel like a cup of milk.

On another note the place is nice and employees are always friendly.

Overpriced, bad wifi, slow service. 
the coffee is so overpriced it's sad. 5 bucks for a teeny tiny itsy bitsy coffee that tastes okay. I ordered a latte and it sat behind the counter for 20 minutes??

One of the first spots we ate that's local to Tampa. The drive through was fast and everyone was really friendly. The food was great and fresh. Also, the house drip coffee black was delicious. I am definitely a black coffee snob and it was wonderful.  Will definitely return!!

Amazing coffee. Amazing service. Get the lazy bread, it's fudgy and sweet, but not too sweet. The perfect pairing with their aero cappuccino. My husband and I were staying nearby and discovered this coffee shop. We've been back 3 times! Travis was so kind, helpful and clearly passionate about what he does! He convinced me to try the Chagaccino, it was yummy and the perfect balance of flavor! Wish this placed existed in NJ where we live. Keep up the great work guys!
Great food, bagel with lox, malteds, greek salad, potato salad, Jewish apple cake, matzo ball soup, all delicious!  Delivery is quick too.
Meh. Mediocre food and overpriced! Spend your money elsewhere.

This is most definitely one of those places that deserves more love. 

The way I saw it on a Sunday morning, there were the places that had a line. Obviously they're all good. People seem to be looking for higher culinary experiences in Rittenhouse Square. 

And honestly, we came to Rachael's because the place I wanted to go to had a line up the street. We just decided to come here instead. 

And I'm actually glad I did. Because we got some decent bacon and eggs and a pretty good bagel sandwich for $10 total. 

Combine this with a quick trip to LaColombe coffee nearby and eat it in the square. It's a perfect combo.
Always great cheese steaks and cheese fries. Super fast service and great folks helping you out.

Amazing -- highly recommend. Better than Dalessandros? Don't @ me. Neighborhood vibe. The women working the counter are so friendly and seem to have a ball working together. 

We had the chicken cheesesteak, fries, and mozz sticks. The chicken was diced thin but still juicy. The bread: meat ratio was perfect! Steak fries were still crispy when I got home.

This was my favorite cheesesteak place when I lived in Philly for 2 years. Definitely a hidden gem only about 25 minutes outside of the city. The food is delicious, delivery was always timely and food was still hot. Also some of the best fries! If you're nearby, definitely check this place out for an authentic cheesesteak, either beef or chicken!

An under the radar gem, this is among my favorite cheesesteaks in the city. Unlike some of their competition there is never a wait, and their steaks are consistently outstanding. In addition to great cheesesteaks they do a great job with their wings and other appetizers so you can easily have a well rounded meal if you're looking for a variety of fried deliciousness. They deliver quickly if you live nearby and it is always an easy option for takeout as well. Overall - if you're looking for a great steak without having to wait all day this is your spot.
Yummmmm. Plant based soft serve with all the toppings you can image. Friendly and delicious! Also bought home made cookies and chia pudding to go.

Amazing. My favorite açaí bowl place in town. Such a cute place and everything I have tried has been delicious. The outside has a chicken coop & lots of plants, making for a fun environment to enjoy a drink/bowl/ice cream!

By far the best smoothie/bowl spot in Tampa. Fresh frozen ingredients without added ice. Clean inside with attention to this detail. Friendly staff and great knowledge of their products. Awesome sitting area outside with show chickens and greenery everywhere. I go here every time I'm in Tampa because it's the best!

I really liked this place. First off, I thought a Wheat grass coffee would be gross and I was wrong. It was actually very tasty. I got it with coconut milk. Also had the açaí bowl and brownie sundae and they were both excellent. Everything was tasty and the staff friendly. I'd certainly be a regular is I lived around here.
The worker was very helpful and gave samples to whatever we wanted to try. A little pricy- but overall worth it.

First of all disgusting food, BLAND no flavor at all, I didn't eat my food it was a waste of money, I ordered a hamburger and boneless wings with fries .... both were nasty chicken was tough burger was bland and fries soggy and nasty I will never return and spend my well earned money on these pieces of shits again!!!!

Quality food with attention to detail. Compared to its counterparts it stands out mainly in its dedication to its namesake . No matter the hour or traffic , this joint has yet to slack off on quality from shift to shift . Most know all to well the perils of these type of establishments (Salems, Zekos, etc.) ; in short Fresh n' Fun  hits its mark.

Come here if you want your food with a huge dash of COVID-19. It is so sad because their food is good, but literally no one wears masks properly. They just sport the masks chin-diaper style with the mask pulled waaaaay below their faces exposing their nose and mouth. Go to Craft Fry instead much more precautions are taken and everything is better. Why go to a restaurant that doesn't value your health/safety? You are literally giving people money to make you sick....think about it.

The menu is chocked full of great options and our selections did not disappoint. The Build Your Own Bowls are fantastic and the breakfast sandwiches are outstanding as well. We will be back every time we visit Tampa.

Super slow on a weekday at 1030am. How long does it take to toast a bagel?
A bit of a language barrier as well to the point that coffee and a bagel seemed hard to understand. 
But the quality kind of makes up for the human rough edges.
For one thing, the interior design is gorgeous. Very comfortable seats and counter stools.
The menu is deliciious when you finally actually get something.
i guess they only do one thing at a time. Dont stop by unless you have time to waste. This isnt a fast spot for anything.
That said, I dont know why anyone would prefer the hideous PDQ next door when this superior alternative beckons.
My iced coffee was high quality .
So was the toasted bagel with dill cream cheese.
Parking is in the back. Dont struggle with Dale Mabry side.

Amazing brunch, the cheese grits are to die for. We were given to us for free by one of the staff members because our friend ordered them and she felt like we needed to try them. If that kind of service alone doesn't make you wanna go there it's a you thing. Also sell mimosas by the bottle. Duh

The food is delicious here and the inside is beautiful too. Staff is pleasant and I've had good overall service...even with pick ups during the worst of the pandemic. 

Today (6.14.21), service is still good. Just a little less table service than I'm use to. No one really checks on you to see if you need a fresh cup of coffee or anything else. Especially since they've created a self serve station with room temperature water, napkins, etc. 

Nevertheless, I do appreciate that the staff still wears mask. Great job on this! Well, except the front cashier....she's maskless...which is probably not a good idea for her.

Food: I love it! Always fresh and presentation is amazing! Happy brunching here as well.

Tip: Coffee drinker love a hot refill...how can we get this table service back to that minimum, at least?!?

Overall: A must try...

Blessings,

KW

This  little gem of a restaurant has all the variety. You can make so many different combinations of a sandwich or a bowl. They have a refrigerator with really cool drinks, and they carry alcohol which makes it nice in case you're in the mood for a champagne brunch. They have vegetarian and vegan options as well and some unusual items like fresh mushrooms. I always love a place that has pickled onions which I threw on my bowl!  The restaurant is clean and the staff are pleasant. Good job Graze
Horrible. Took 2 hours for delivery and my pizza was cold when it got here. I called for them to rectify the situation. Basically they told me it was nothing they can do.

Man, I really don't enjoy leaving negative reviews but these wings were especially bad. 
They were all very tiny, and therefore super dry. I felt like I was chewing tiny bits of sandpaper. Half of the bones were broken & they are definitely frozen (black bones). I also got this tiny little nub thing instead of a 10th wing so that was a bummer. 

The sauce (nuclear & suicide) were both good with a nice kick hence the 2 stars.  

We ordered delivery and it was pretty pricey too- for the cost I was expecting some decent size wings (& to get all my 10 wings vs a weird nubbin).

Amazing! Pizza is delicious! Wings are great! Service and Delivery is always quick and satisfying! Colonial's Cheese Pizza and Buffalo Chicken Pizza are a must try! Trust you won't be disappointed! Excuse the Photo I couldn't wait to indulge!
The best Gyro in town.  When I crave a Gyro there are no other like La Pita's Gyros.  The bread, meat, and Tzatziki sauce are perfect.  Thank you for doing it right!

We had gyros, the veggie platter, tabbouleh, Potatoes & chicken/lamb combo platter.  Everything was amazing, best we've had since we moved here from Ohio.  I've been searching for a good tabbouleh for years and I've finally found it! The gyro was so good my 12yr old requested I make this account to leave a proper 5 review.

I just had the Chicken Tikka Masala here and this is my takeaway:

1. The chicken tikka masala tasted almost nothing like what I used to get in California. From San Diego to Artesia, I loved the chicken tikka masala I had everywhere in SoCal. This tasted weird and it was difficult to eat.

2. It took about 40 minutes from when I ordered the food to have it ready. This is a Wednesday night and it is far from busy. There was just one family dining in and about two other people picked up food while I was there. How did it take 40 minutes to make my food? I think they waited til I was there before they started making it.

3. It costs $16 for a single chicken breast and a cup of rice.

I will not be going back.

Had a good takeout experience and enough of a reason to justify an updated review! This time I called in my order of Butter chicken and naan (instead of using the online system). I was provided an estimated wait time of 40 minutes with an explanation that they had to run out of rice; a long wait but it was somewhat reassuring that they had been busy enough to run out of rice. 
I planned accordingly and upon arriving only had to wait about 3 to 5 minutes for my food to be brought out. The portions were huge! The order contained enough chicken and rice to turn my one order into two meals - and hands down, Tikka Masala makes the best butter chicken in the T&C area.

Best Indian restaurant in Tampa Bay. I've waited to write this review and can say that the best part is the food is not only tasty but has been consistently good. I've now eaten here 10+ times. I've also eaten at almost every Indian restaurant in Tampa and most either don't try very hard or are hit or miss depending on the day. 

Give this place a try; they will earn your business. 

To top it off, the owner is nice and the service has been good when I sat in.

I wrote a rave review recently, and some friends have visited a couple of times since.  But this is a report from their last visit a few days ago - two ladies for lunch.
The food was still excellent, BUT before going I would now call them to verify that they have enough staff, because my friends had a bad experience.  One guy and a kid helper who didn't help much.  People would come and wait 1/2 hour and hadn't ordered yet and left.   And I'd tell them that unless I saw at least someone in the kitchen and another competent person out front that I would leave.  And tell them that I would check the bathrooms and unless they were clean, I would leave.  No light in the ladies room, and told to use the men's room which was too disgusting to describe here.  A restaurant inspector once told me that regulations don't allow you to go in the kitchen at a restaurant, but if you look in the bathroom, that's an indicator of the cleanliness of the kitchen.  
It's awfully tough for restaurants to survive in these covid days, but unless you could verify on the phone in advance that those aspects were OK, you should not go, and then verify when you got there that they really were OK in order to stay.

Was there today, largely based on 5 star rating on Yelp, and that's what I rated it also.
A gigantic menu - maybe 15 vegetarian appetizers + non-vegetarian.  Pages and pages of choices.
We had an eggplant appetizer - I think it was #14 - terrific.  And some garlic naan bread - doesn't get any better.
Main courses:  butter chicken and some kind of goat dish in a brown sauce - both excellent.
We had about 1/2 of each entree, so there was a lot to take home.
Service very courteous and intelligent.
I like Indian music well enough, but this was sort of a continuous rap/hip-hop version.  Almost annoying enough for me to make this review 4 stars.

Horrible service. Waited for an hour on a pick up order when they said it would be 25 minutes only. Not busy at all. When i arrived they told me they didn't have something instead of telling me on the phone. Then when I received my food, it was all thrown in the to go box. And still didn't get the order correct. Ask for them to correct it and they STILL messed up. Very frustrating. Should do better! Very disappointed, especially since this is suppose to be the "SJU" bar you'd think things would be better. As a employee of SJU, you'd think yall would treat people better and have better service. Wasted my money. Food was cold also!! Smh.

The fish tacos were terrible. They missing half the ingredients and nothing like the picture or description. There wasn't any sauce on them, sour cream included, a lime to give its dry fish stick seasoning, and instead of the cabbage, they gave me soggy lettuce. fries were soggy and cold too. The short rib on the Mac n cheese was completely dry and flavorless. The best part of all of this was we wrote in that we were staying at the Hilton, and they didn't include any utensils or napkins. It's covid. Room service is outlawed. They didn't have utensils to give us so try eating Buffalo Mac n cheese and short rib Mac n cheese with your hands. I'm furious.

My experience was terrible the server Dani today was not attentive to us at all. We finished our appetizers before our entrees came. When she dropped off our entrees the appetizers was never removed then we had to eat around the appetizers due to limited table space. She barely barely came came and checked on us and when we asked for the check she dropped it off and didnt come back at all to take the payments for over 10 minutes. I went to the front to pay and they said i couldnt i have to pay with the server. I just paid cash and left due to the negative experience i was having which made me more frustrated. Then i got charged a 20 Percent gratuity which I understand but I believe maybe that why i was not getting good service at all. It was not packed in there at all so that is no excuse

Stopped by Landmark last night and overall it was a great time catching up with my friends who I barely get to go out with. We all ordered a drink or two, I had the lemon drop martini which was pretty good and I also got a mango mojito with grey goose instead of Bacardi and that was fire! For my meal I had the jerk salmon caesar salad which was more well done than I would have liked it to be but whatever I still ate it; however my friends all enjoyed their meals. My only complaint would be that the host placed us on an hour wait just for us to get seated and be rushed when ordering our food. The kitchen stopped accepting orders which I felt was a bit rude considering they closed at 12AM and stopped accepting food orders at 10:45PM. I personally felt that the server was trying to hurry up and get off work maybe, but regardless my night would've been more enjoyable if it wasn't rushed. Next time I will just come earlier but this place used to be known for its late night dining, doesn't seem like the place for that anymore.

This long established restaurant at one time was a "go to" in Northeast Philadelphia. I don't know how such a complete downfall could have happened so quickly. We ordered takeout last night. I had flounder listed as "fresh atlantic flounder platter". She gave me the bag at the curbside, and it felt light. I drove 2 blocks and checked it. Inside were 2 pieces of fish approx 2" x 3" cold. That was it. I took them back, she apologized and brought back 2 extra small containers 1 cole slaw, i apple sauce. All this for $21. Complete disappointing ripoff. We will NOT be returning. Avoid this place folks. The pic is in the smallest size take away foil

Used to love this place the food was underwhelming tonight. Let's just say the Broccoli, steamed broccoli looked better than most everything on the plates. Most of it just looked blah except for the salmon dinner which looked good. The soda was flat and tasted bad. The service wasn't that great either felt like we were forgotten several times during meal. To top it off I couldn't find some one to pay my bill I almost thought I had to pay at bar mind you this was after getting the bill 15 minutes before. All in all either it was an off night or just not what it used to be. Best thing about the meal was the people around the table.

Turned away around 5pm at the takeout section on Mothers Day telling me they're not taking any more orders. Took the bus there to get dinner for my mother and I. A message on Facebook saying you weren't taking any more orders would have been nice. Absolutely ruined the holiday for us. The last time I was there and actually able to buy food, I noticed they added I think it was a $3 surcharge to the bill when picking up from takeout. Thanks for that during a pandemic when your business seems to be thriving. I'm 48 and have been taken to this restaurant since I can remember. Not like it used to be. Better off getting seafood steamed at supermarkets now.

This place is deceiving.  The outside is really nice. The food...is Jersey shore, Boardwalk quality. I started with the fried calamari. There was more fried batter and pepper rings than there was calamari. Then I had the shrimp sampler. The stuffed crab was broiled on top but not cooked on the underside. There were lots of crab shells in it. The scampi was a thick, soupy consistency and actually tasted like chicken broth. And I've never seen shrimp fried and split like that. My husband had the glazed salmon. It was cooked perfectly-but even with the glaze, it tasted like nothing. Red bliss potatoes-seasoned with nothing. Best part of the meal was the artificial lemonade. For the prices, I expected a much better quality.

4pm reservation.. 45 minutes later they gave our table to someone else. Then they sit a 5pm reservation the moment they walk in because they know the manager. Staff with no masks. Kitchen have no masks. Bus boys no masks. Just a joke

My husband ordered from here and gave his debit card number to an employee over the phone for an order. A couple days later, he noticed miscellaneous charges on his card, including 2 food purchases from this restaurant A coincidence? I don't think so.
