We said mild spicy but it didn't have any spice at all! I also asked them what they do for birthday and they said they bring dessert. They brought the Thai donut yum with a candle. I will return here. Thank you for the great service

Excellent dining experience, perfect afternoon outing in Downtown. Located just a couple blocks from the river walk, there is plenty of indoor and outdoor seating.

I had the chef special fish and salad. Thai Iced team and a Singha!

I don't know if it's southern food with East coast influences or something else. What I do know is that Honey's has delicious food prepared with care. Wonderful crispy latkes served with breakfast and some seriously strong coffee will get your day (along with your colon) moving.

The breakfast is decent. Long line but it moves quick. The service is great and the bathrooms are clean. We order the egg benedicts with asparagus and ham - this dish is excellent. Their french toast is yummy too.

Ordered the Honey Cristo with a side of potato latkes and a cup of fruit. The honey cristo was sweet, savory, and even more delicious when paired with their in-house maple syrup and berry preserve. The latke had the perfect consistency and I could see why people rave about it. Even the fruit was fresh and well portioned. On the whole, I would rank this meal as one of my favorite breakfasts in Philadelphia. Five stars - Highly recommend.

Came here for brunch and ordered the huevos rancheros and chicken and waffles. I loved the huevos rancheros! Especially the egg that they cooked just right cuz some restaurants don't know how to not overcook their eggs. My boyfriend got the chicken and waffles, which he wasn't a huge fan of. Said the waffles just tasted like frozen waffles from the grocery store and the chicken was bland and had too much breading. I can say that I wasn't wowed either, although the chicken was not that bad.

Forgot to tell you that I've eaten here twice in the past couple of days. I was able to get seated immediately.  Hostess was awesome as well as both servers.

This review specifically is going to be about my brunch today. Ordered the Honeys play with Challah French Toast, crispy bacon, potato pancake and scrambled eggs!  Had an orange juice and some water.  Ate outside in the "park lette" as the call it now.

Food was perfectly cooked to order and again service was amazing.

Still the spot to "Find  Old  Tampa"  (full disclaimer: I'm biased here as sixteen years ago I spent time living above the place with a wildly fun group of friends...) Yet Still .The Place.  Journey through True  History of Old  Tampa while staying in the present moment.. even if cigars may not be your choice... come here during a sunny afternoon for the beverage that you do seek and the vibe will layer you richly. THE KING!!!
Our group only had time for one cigar, but the coffee and breakfast sandwich were outstanding, as was the outside seating and people watching that morning.  I'll definitely be back.

The food was delicious . It's been a while so glad I am glad that I found this restaurant. This is the aftermath lol  I  don't usually  eat so much in one seating but I could  not stop. 
 
Definitely coming back!

Delicious food all around and some of the best Griot I've ever had! Coming from South Florida and my husband being Haitian, we have the difficult struggle of finding good Haitian food when we came to Tampa. Drove here on a whim because I read that they had Kremas. Unfortunately, they did not have Kremas when I arrived but I ordered food: Griot, Akras, Legume, and Oxtail. Everything was fantastic! My husband and I are happy in a food coma and will definitely be ordering here again! Also, PRESTIGE!!!

It really is as amazing as everyone says it is! We were lucky to score a seat on the patio on a Friday night for a special occasion. We absolutely loved everything on the tasting menu, from the salatim to the chicken, branzino, and lamb shoulder. The service was top notch. There was a lot of food so come hungry! Hope to be able to come back soon.

Great experience! Besides the far out reservation it was all worth the wait. Food is delicious, service is top tier, and the environment is great! Solomonov was there at the time and even came by to check on us. Very pleasant and kind. Made the experience that much better. Highly recommended

Standout dish: Hummus 5/5
Service 5/5
Starters 4/5
Entrees 3/5
Dessert 3.3/5
Wine pairings 2/5

Tip:  Seating by the bar at 5:30PM or 9:00PM is usually available on Resy. People also tend to cancel their reservations so if you request to be notified of an opening, you can score a table a day or 2 ahead of your desired time and reservation date. If you also plan to order the chef's tasting menu, come knowing you will be stuffed. My party couldn't finish everything so we had to pack a lot in take-out boxes. If you're eco-conscious, pack a couple tupperware with you. It was a ridiculous amount of food. 

I've traveled to many Michelin starred restaurants and James beard winners... and I found Zahav to be good but overrated. The hype doesn't match the ridiculous 1-2 month reservation sell-out craze. I'm not sure if this was an off night or what but their starters were far more enjoyable than their main dishes. It started going downhill once we got our lamb shoulder. The lamb shoulder was juicy and tender but it was too rich and thick for our liking. The accompanying Persian rice didn't help offset the richness. The drink that is paired with the dessert came off sweet and cloying. Thankfully my server listened and poured me a different glass that paired better with our dessert. 

On the other hand, is chef Michael Solomonov running a Miss/Mr. Confidentiality pageant for his FOH? My servers were great. The path to the bathroom from the bar was a bit tight so I bumped into at least 6 different servers/bussers and they were all nice. Even when we were leaving the restaurant, there was a line of incredibly friendly servers who gave us a pleasant send-off. 

Would I come back? Only for their perfect hummus but I'll try recreating it at home. Scoring a table was highly inconvenient and my dining experience here wasn't worth the extra effort.

TDLR; Get that bread, get that hummus, then leave. Peace out.

There have been many moments in my life where I questioned my intelligence, but never as much as when I think about the fact that I never went to Zahav when I literally lived in Philly and then took a few more years afterward to finally go. BUT I FINALLY DID IT after waking up early to finesse a 9:30pm Saturday reservation.

Even at such a late time, it was truly poppin'. We waited outside on the patio and I must have visibly perked up when our name was called because the host noted, "You seem excited!" which led to conversation about my regret about missing out on the Zahav experience but finally making my way over from the west coast. 

We were seated in a booth inside where the lighting was dim and warm. Whoever was on aux that night was on point because it was blasting hip hop and R&B the whole night (my friend and I tried to recreate a Zahav playlist afterward). 

At the time, only the chef's tasting menu was available. Initially, I misunderstood the situation to be that we chose one option per course but then the waiter came by to explain that (to my delight) it would be everything on the menu! 

There's just a TRAIN of neverending food (although they do give you a little break in the middle to digest) so I'll make note of my personal standouts:
-Salatim: Six vegetable salads of beet, carrot, eggplant, fennel, and more. The flavors were bold and sharp and I loved all the different textures involved here. This (the first dish of the first course) is the point at which I knew I was overestimating my stomach space.
-Laffa bread with hummus-tehina: Love at first sight when I saw giant bread coming with the plate of artfully swirled hummus with a shiny pool of olive oil and sunburst of spices. The soft bread itself was studded with herbs itself and, when combined with the hummus, was mindblowing. We finished the laffa before the hummus but luckily they later brought us even more (at no extra charge). 
-Haloumi: I'm a cheese lover and this felt like a classy version of the string cheese of my youth that I would microwave until it got a little crispy on the edges - the haloumi was golden and crispy on the outside and topped with strawberry matbucha (which is like a cooked tomato/bell pepper dip), pickled rhubarb, and green almond, so you can imagine what a flavor explosion that was. The strawberry provided just the right amount of sweetness to balance everything out.
-Maitake mushroom: I'm allergic to walnuts, so they actually gave us two full servings of this dish - one with and without. There was a good smoky char flavor and it was not rubbery whatsoever.
-Pomegranate lamb shoulder with crispy persian rice: This was probably my favorite, and I say this even though I only had a few bites (I struggled to even make it this far). The lamb (I already like lamb though) was incredibly juicy and tender, falling apart with a little nudge. It was reminiscent of hongshao rou (Chinese red braised pork dish that I adore with my entire being) which also has a sweet, glossy glaze on top. The crispy rice surprised me because it wasn't like the crispy rice you get at, for example, the bottom of a Korean dolsot which sticks together/on your teeth as you chew it; rather, the persian crispy rice had a lighter, fleeting presence as you ate it. Of course, the flavors were also delicious and softened the heaviness of the lamb.
-Tehina semifreddo: Of course, there's always room for dessert. This was creamy and mild with a subtle salt note in the chocolate. 
-Konafi: Something I had never tried but loved the combination of nutty, buttery, and fruity flavors. 

Throughout the meal there were a couple different servers who were all funny, friendly, and able to anticipate our needs before we even knew them ourselves. Chef Solomonov also came out personally at the end to greet us and someone had told him that I was visiting which was a nice touch. He was so friendly and I was a little starstruck. 

We left with stacks of leftovers and absolutely bursting stomachs. Zahav is the restaurant of dreams!

Ok where do I start? We travel to Philly often because it is only 1.5 hours away from NYC, didn't realize the first time how hard it was to get a reservation here and after having our first meal last night I finally understand.  My photos will explain everything with the prix fix menu but I just want to say that I have never I mean NEVER had hummus that smooth and creamy as well as the Laffa bread that crispy and fluffy at the same time.  The rice that looks like a cake was definitely a surprise.  Everything else was so tasty and refine that I say it is worth the wait.  The portion may seem small at first because it is tasting menu style but in the end we were stuffed and it was very satisfying.  Staff was professional and courteous and made this birthday celebration for my husband memorable.
Once again another satisfied customer.  This place never dissapoints. Brought my family here from Savannah & they enjoyed their double decker burgers. They kept saying how juicy & delicious it was.
Good service and good bar food....lively atmosphere as well...Right next to our hotel so we walked....I would return, especially if I'm in the mood for some wings and a cold brew.

Well of course I turned to Yelp to assist me with this transition to Tampa. I was approached by the Waitress Karlee(Twin) who sat me in my section. The place was semi-busy due to a party that will be taking place as she explained to me: there is a contactless QR menu and a physical drink menu. I ordered the wings as suggested along with the Buffalo shrimp as a starter. My drinks were the Tropical Storm. This place was a good choice and food was great. I secondly will come back. Don't forget to end the night with a green tea shot! ‍

Atmosphere - Very good. The restaurant has lots of televisions, with various channels playing. There is a large covered patio that also has lots of TVs. 

Service - Decent. Our server was pleasant and attentive.

Food - Good. I ordered a club sandwich. The sandwich had lots of meat, but it tasted somewhat dry, which I would attribute to thick Texas toast. The bonus for me was that one of the sides offered is tater tots and they were excellent. 

Overall Value - Above Average. The prices are reasonable and the quality of food and service would rate above what I would expect from a sports bar.

Covid Practices - masks are required for customers entering the restaurant. Our server wore a mask at all times and wore it correctly.

Looking for an outdoor place to eat near Busch Gardens and discovered this place.  It is a Sports Bar in he respect there are TV's everywhere and tuned into different stations.  The outside patio has guests spread out, which is what we wanted.   We were actually the only ones there for lunch.

The menu is varied, with appetizers, salads, burgers and sandwiches.    Prices were comparable to restaurants of this type.  

Our server was quick to provide menus and bring us our drinks, and then to take our order.   I opted for the patty melt with fries.    She asked what temperature for the burger and I responded with medium well.   We didn't wait long for our food,  but when presented, mine was extremely pink, so certainly not medium well.   Not being a fan of pink ground meat, I asked our server to please have them cook it longer.   When it was returned minutes later, I could tell they had pulled the burger off, stuck it in the microwave and then put it back on the bread.   There was no flavor, couldn't taste the thousand island dressing and very few onions.    Super disappointing.  The fries were nothing special.

Not a great experience, so am doubtful to return, even though we are at Busch Gardens often and don't care for their food.

tl;dr this no-frills  eatery has you set for bun bo hue and other Vietnamese comfort food delights

While most folks are familiar with pho, have you tried bun bo hue? Literally translating to "Hue beef noodle soup," this dish is the cousin of pho but bears a few notable differences. Firstly, bun bo hue operates with a pork-based broth, unlike pho which is typically chicken or beef stock. In addition, Bun bo hue broth is typically spicier and heartier, flavored by chili oil, lemongrass, shrimp paste, and annatto, and classically topped with braised beef, Vietnamese ham, and tendon. Lastly, bun bo hue utilizes thick vermicelli noodles, as opposed to flat noodles (i.e., the literal translation of "pho"). Now that you're well-versed in your Vietnamese soup game, let's get to the review: Philly's premier bun bo hue kitchen, Cafe Diem.

A gaudy sign alerts you to the restaurant, which otherwise looks like a normal rowhome from the street view. Once within, the flavorful aromas starkly contrast the frill-less decor: cool-toned lighting fixtures, faux marble tabletops, fake plants, and grout-less stone tile walls all scream "hole-in-the-wall" more than "dining destination." The narrow dining room stretched back surprisingly far and is crammed with tables, each more likely than not taken by locals.

On a chilly spring day, my partner and I trekked through the drizzle over to Cafe Diem. We were greeted with a pot of tea as we browsed the menus. We started with a Vietnamese Iced Coffee, then opted for the Bun Bo Hue and the Banh Cuon (crepe-like rice sheet rolls). The coffee was espresso-strong, with the characteristic sweetness of condensed milk. Our enormous bowl of soup, heavy on the meat, should be filed under the definition of "comfort food." All the intricacies of pho were compounded with the moderate spice and all-around heartiness characteristic of bun bo hue, generating the perfect cold-weather food. And don't let the tendon deter you --  slow cooking in the broth leaves the rich tendon slices very nearly melting in your mouth. Meanwhile, the banh cuon, a dish that lies somewhere between dumplings and spring rolls, proved an ideal pairing. Filled with meat slices and topped with rich and salty Vietnamese ham slices and served with a sweet and sour dipping sauce, each roll provided a similar, yet complementary, array of flavors to the soup.

Service was quick and courteous without being overbearing. Of note, cash only, and closes somewhat early (6:30pm) each day!

At ~$30 total for our meal, Cafe Diem proved to be a rip-roaring deal. Although somewhat of a hike, I will be back here when a hankering for solid soup kicks in.
Best bun bo hue spot in Philly without a doubt.  Had to drop by this place after picking up grocery at the local Asian markets.

This spot has really good bun bo hue, but I've been noticing that their waitress and a few other workers do not wash their hands or wear their mask when they serve you. It's scary for me mostly because I'm currently pregnant and not vaccinated. I don't think I want to return here for a while just for my safety... I don't want them to lose business for this, but it is very upsetting to see a business lacking care and sensitivity for others during this tough time.

Their broth is god tier. Bun bo hue is one of my favorite foods and this place is the real deal. The broth was super spicy but full of so much flavor. They also give a lot of meat. The only reasons I give it a 4 instead of a 5: there was no porks blood which I feel like is normally included in bun bo hue. Same with banana flower. Also, they didn't seem super mindful of covid conditions. Pretty cramped and operating at full capacity. Also, might ask for spice on the side next time. It was VERY spicy.
Always a classic been here more than 20X over the the last decade and great food and amazing service is always expected as well as deliverered.  Can't go wrong with a night out at Berns.

This place is impressive. That's undeniable. Brant was our waiter and did an amazing job. Extremely attentive and on top of everything. I ordered my steak rare and when it came out it was just a bit over done. It still tasted great. If I had cooked it myself I would have eaten it happily but he saw the look on my face. (I hate sending things back.) He insisted on it and had another out to me in moments that was absolutely perfect. Then the experience went downhill. My party went up to the famous dessert room. We were having a blast and were greeted immediately. Put our orders in. Nearly 30 mins went by and I still didn't have my drink. As I went to the bathroom I mentioned to a member of the staff that our drinks hadn't arrived. He gave me a look and said we cut you guys off. I was taken aback as I was absolutely not close to that level, nor was anyone in my party. Not to mention I would think a manager would have handled that kind of thing. I wouldn't know as I've never been told that in my 18 years of being over 21. I asked to speak to the manager and she insulted me by serving me a small glass filled to the top with ice as if I wouldn't notice. It was very apparent to everyone that they just wanted to go home as it was late. Very disappointed how it ended with such a crash. We would have been happy to leave if they had just said they were closing instead of pushing us to leave through unprofessional tactics. Would have been 6 stars for the first hour we were there. A shame to spend over a thousand dollars between the 6 of us and have it end like that.

This is a delayed review. We've been to Bern's multiple times. My kids love it because of the ambiance and they can dress up. The last time we were there was probably the last, because of a not so good experience with the service. We felt we were rushed, and the server was kind of condescending with inappropriate remarks. It was a special occasion, that's the only reason I did not "engage". The food is what you expect, every steak comes with the soup, salad and vegetables. Only this time soup and vegetables were lukewarm. After dinner we went to the dessert room. Same kind of service, rushed and MIA server. The only time she came back was during the middle of our dessert to leave the check. We were not done and was going to get coffee, but since she brought the check without asking we decided to stop ordering. Disappointing, but time to move on and find a new "favorite" restaurant.

2.5 stars but rounded up due to the fact Kenny playing the piano was great. Drinks in the lounge were really good but once we went to the dessert room the quality went down hill . The service in the dessert room was non existent, we were shuffled by 2 servers and one kept blaming the other. For the prices and wait I was expecting something special . The carrot cake was okay but the ice cream was fantastic! The the fact the lounge/ bar was so busy and the service was better than the slow desert room is insane. Would never waste my time on the dessert room again.

What a unique experience here. This place is quite the establishment in Tampa. It could be pretentious and way way overpriced, but I didn't get that impression at all. Our server was so kind and attentive, treated us just like family. Food was delicious. And of course, the dessert room is such a cool thing too. You have to go at least once in Tampa for a special occasion or just for a wonderful meal! Thank you!

We came in on July 4th because we were having lunch close by and on their window they are advertising a July 4th special with a medium drink and a mousse cake for $9.00. once we came in, the girl at the registry said she knows nothing about the special that is posted on the window. Bait and switch?!  That explains why we are the only ones inside the store while all other restaurants around this area are buzzing. Wonder how long they are going to last

T cafe never fails to amaze. Today we got a custom birthday cake. I will say the flavor is quite subtle. I think it could do with a little more sugar in the cake and the icing. However, if you don't have a sweet tooth but want a cake, this is great for you. We choose the pink ombré icing, plain vanilla cream, vanilla cake, and fresh strawberries. On top we're fruit, candy, and waffle cones filled with two different flavored creams: mango and red tea. 

Although the price is quite steep at $55 the packaging and beauty of this cake is well worth it if you want to go for a show stopper. 

I've also tried their crepe cakes here and they are really delicious. My favorite is the mango, but the matcha is great as well. Those are $11 each but they are pure heaven.

We got our food from the food truck while it was at Wissahickon Brewery. We ordered the Brisket Cheesesteak and Beer Cheese Fries and they did NOT disappoint! The brisket was cooked to perfection and was incredibly flavorful. The only downside was the portion of the fries was a bit small, we definitely wanted more. We highly recommend this place! We will absolutely be back.
If I could put 0 stars I would. Stinks, looks dirty. Employees were talking in the back and ignoring me as I tried to pick up my order. Avoid at all costs.

Deke's forgot part of our order and when I called to let them know I ended up hanging up after being placed on hold for 7 minutes.  The food was below average based on the potato wedges being cold and seemed like they were set out of a long time, and the brisket being dry.  The positives for me were the way they package the food and it being a cool hole in the wall vibe.

Had heard great things about the ribs and decided to order from the Berkley st location. Very disappointed. Ribs were not moist at all, asked for extra sauce but there wasn't enough to dip a piece of bread in. Maybe it was a bad night for them but wouldn't recommend them. I live in the neighborhood and try to support local but not this time. A waste of 34$

Fairly priced. Online ordering experience easy. High points: brisket, pork ribs, and hush puppies. Don't waste your time: collard greens and banana pudding. Especially the banana pudding. I don't know who recipe that was or who brilliant idea it was not include banana or whole nilla wafers should be cancelled lol. Hunny what y'all have is NOT banana pudding and y'all should just take it off ASAP. But kiss the cook for that amazing brisket and ribs.

This food is phenomenal. Walk past the other restaurants on 7th, and stroll a little further down. You will not regret it. We had chicken, Mac and cheese, wings, potato salad, and peach cobbler. Every single thing was great. To make it even more enticing, the workers are fun, friendly, and efficient.
I came to this Pokeworks couples of times and they are all great experiences. The cashier was very friendly and helpful. Food is delicious and fish were fresh. Will definitely coming back

I've been coming to Pokeworks since they opened and boy have they gone downhill. Avocado is over ripe and black and they're serving it. The crab salad was dry and look like it's been sitting out all day. The other vegetables were not fresh at all, Wilted. The white rice was OK. The best thing about my meal was the delicious stone fruit tea that they serve in the fountain container. However, I will not be coming back to this establishment this is the 2nd time I got low quality poke.

Love this place. The toppings are really fresh and they're unlimited! The price is fair considering all the add ons. The surimi salad is so good and they have lots of options for protein. Some other reviews mention places nearby that are cheaper, but every other place I've tried gives you maybe 3-4 toppings and it's practically the same price as here. You can literally get 15+ toppings for $12 so it's sooo worth it compared to other places. It's also very filling and I can barely finish the bowl. Definitely try this place out.

Stop over for lunch before my next class. I had the spicy tuna and spicy salmon, kelp salad, edamame, Serrano aoli, yuzu ponzu sauce, fried onions and garlic, jalapeños, corn and rice. Overall it was good but the scoops of the fish are sooooo tiny, I kinda wish the scoops were bigger for the price and I also wanted more sauces. The sauces sounded so good lol. The fish was fresh and all the ingredients tasted fresh as well.

It was my first time here and I truly didn't know what to order but Shaq took his time and help me with a great tasting bowl! I will truly come back because of the service and food!! Thank you Shaq  you rock!! Also I already ate the food no photos to show

It's challenging to find good Jamaican food! I believe Dezzy's is one of the good ones and was worth the drive!

If you love Jamaican food, most locations look typically the same -- just like this one. There was a bit of a line inside when I arrived but not too, too long of a wait. The people that work there were nice.

I ordered a medium sized jerk chicken platter with: jerk sauce on top, rice & peas, cabbage, and plantain. I was impressed! The jerk was not that spicy but good (I'm not big on spicy spicy). Also purchased a Jamaican cream soda and cornbread (cornbread was not homemade; did not enjoy).

I see that they offer breakfast! I would like to try that next!

We had dinner last night 7/2/21 at the Columbus Blvd. location and let me tell you the food was ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE!!!! I ordered clams and black mussels together with a garlic butter sauce. My food came out wrapped in a plastic bag. At first I thought I was given someone else's take-out order. The bartender, who was great, informed me that is how the dish is served. Ok, so after unwrapping it I looked at my seafood and saw that it was covered in huge chunks of raw garlic. The same for my husbands entree. He went through the task of scraping off the garlic just to eat it. A guest should not have to do that. I could barely get through mine. Doesn't anyone in management look ,let alone taste any of the food coming out of that kitchen!!! I like garlic but not chunks of it, enough to give anyone an upset stomach. We sat in a booth in the bar. We didn't want to sit in the dining room because it was empty, dirty, and the lighting was dark.The only good thing about my experience here was the clam chowder, the cocktails, and the bartender. I would include her name but I forgot it. She was amazing and very sympathetic!!!
Food never arrived.  I was so hopeful, but even a $200 order wasn't important enough for the delivery company OR the restaurant to care.  What a disappointment.

Food wasn't  that good. Service was good. Disappointing  the menu is confusing.  Not a good experience.  The place is clean and spaced out for Covid. Inside dining  is comfortable.  That's  all I  really  have to say.I  didn't  enjoy  my first visit.  I don't  believe  I'll  go back. I don't  eat crabs  but the people  who were eating  crabs seemed  happy.

The food was delicious and a great place to eat but beware of the owner. Mr . Paul . He is the worst person I ever met. The way he talks to staff members and treat customers is not right . I didn't know about the Groupon policy . I drove two hours to try their seafood but after the experience with the owner it just left a sour taste. Avoid this place if you want a place you feel welcome . People make mistakes and as a person you should not fault someone for not knowing but rather to teach and move on . He was so rude to the manager , and the girl in front of us . Would you tell a guest you are losing money in front of them? And just tell a manger to get on the waiter's ass. In front of the customer. Mr Paul shouldn't be a owner to a beautiful establishment. He will bring down the whole establishment.
The crabmeat Fries are perfect! The seafood boil is amazing they let you choose what you want in it along with some extras had the right amount of seasoning and was reasonably priced def recommend

Came here with a friend at the time to get some pastries and coffee. The person working counter may have been new or was getting into the groove of things, but he mixed up a lot of our orders at first. My friend stated that she wanted our orders separate, but they were all included together. Then, the lemon tart I ordered was placed in her bag and not mine, so we ended up sorting that out ourselves. In fairness to him too, there seemed to be only two people working at the time.

The almond croissant was a-okay. Not the most amazing thing I've had, but certainly not the worst. Layers of butter and dough were there and the filling was quite nice, not sickly sweet. The lemon tart was also okay. Honestly I feel it's basically a lemon bar in a cute shape with some meringue piped in a circle that was torched on top. It was a scorcher of a day, and sounded the most refreshing at the time, but maybe I just ordered wrong.

Overall, a nice little place to stop by if you're craving pastries, but I wouldn't say after my first visit it's a destination sort of place.

3.5 stars
Loved the service here! Best thing so far was the croissants! Cold brew was 7/10, but I would go back just because of the atmosphere!

I'd give this place 10 stars if I could. The customer service was over the top and the staff were so cheery and welcoming. You could tell they enjoy coming to work. The latte in the picture isn't from there but I got the smoked salmon with spinach on a baguette. The baguette itself was delicious, it felt like I was back in Paris all over again. I've been searching for smoked salmon on a baguette for years trying to recreate that experience when I was in Europe and this was by far the closest I've gotten. Everything was great quality.
The views are also great, it's nice having the buildings engulf your sight while you're eating. 
ALSO! I left my drink there for some reason and I actually came back to get it and they had saved it for me!!! Like how sweet is that? And the owner was cracking jokes about it. Small stuff like that seems so insignificant but I swear it brightened up my day. Made my crazy life more bearable!! Best way to gain a returning customer. Be sure to check them our, you won't be disappointed!!
Great atmosphere! The pastries look delicious the second you walk in, really friendly staff :)

Super cute place in Philadelphia. Picked up some pastries for breakfast. Place was very clean. Staff member was wearing a mask. Masks were not enforced for vaccinated customers. Croissants were $3/each which were amazingly delicious. So we're the raisin rolls. We also got the baguette which tasted gray as well. We literally wanted every item in there. I'm sure they also taste great!

The food is authentic, solid, Cuban food. Our favorite is the Cuban sandwich and yucca fries. They come with a green sauce that is beyond amazing. BUT, the best part about this place is their Sangria. At 5 bucks a drink, you cannot beat this seriously refreshing drink. They always have a classic sangria, but then also do a yummy seasonal like  peach rose, margarita, or apple cider. I literally bring people who are visiting to Armature works for these drinks bc they are delicious and won't break the bank!!

Plenty of seating when we dined at 3pm. The manager was working the bar so we sat there and our food came out relatively quickly. I ordered a glass of the sangria which was packed with fresh fruit and you could definitely taste it. It was happy hour too and the taste was bomb. I ordered the Hemingway Cuban and the sauce was on point, bread was incredibly pillowy. We had no idea what yucca French fries were but I describe it like eating fried dough. Overall good experience and left full.

This was a favorite. Lately though the service is so-so and the kitchen is variable. Some days the food is great and others it's old, cold, and mediocre. There's no pattern to it, and nothing's more frustrating in a restaurant than inconsistency. I'll probably stay away for a while.

Kuba is now Hemingway's Cuban Kitchen. I loved Kuba and I love Hemingway's just as much. The menu is very similar with some additions including the bowls.  I do like their Cuban Sandwiches; however, the Cuban really isn't one of my favorites there.  My absolute favorite on the menu is La Frita Cubana. La Frita Cubana has a patty made from a house blend of chorizo, pork, and beef. This delicious sandwich is  dressed with perfectly sautéed caramelized onions, melted Swiss cheese, and crispy potato strings in between two, sweet, and yummy, egg buns. I always get the Yuca fries because they are AMAZING and probably the part of the meal that I enjoy the most!  I like me some coffee and their Cafe Con Leche and Cortadito are both delicious. They do have a bar that can seat about five or six people. The service has always been good. It takes awhile to get the food but they're making it fresh so I don't mind waiting.  They give you a buzzer so you can walk around Armature Works or sit down and relax until your food is ready.  This is definitely a place to check out if you're in Armature Works!

Perfect quick stop for breakfast.
Cuban Breakfast sandwich is fresh and delicious. Staff friendly and helpful.

We had a yummy lunch at Taps recently. It was a Saturday (or was it Sunday?) before venturing out to the children's museum across the street. I love the location because you there is plenty of parking with the Poe Garage nearby, and we always need a bite to eat when visiting the museum or the other attractions near Curtis Hixon.

We tried the crab cakes, baked meatballs, bacon wrapped jalapenos, the soft pretzel, and a kid's pizza. 

Our favorite dish was unanimously the jalapenos. They were so flavorful, not too spicy, and came with a yummy dipping sauce. I would order this every visit. It was a pretty large portion as well--4 jalapenos. 

The crab cakes were not my favorite, they could have been larger and had more crab meat. It seemed like a lot of filler, so I would skip these next time. 

The meatballs were good in theory, but they were dense. Either mixed too much, or cooked too long. I would skip those as well. But they did come with cheesy garlic bread, which I would love to be able to order by themselves.

The soft pretzel was great, I just didn't like that we got upcharged for the beer cheese, because by the way it's written on the menu, it looks like it's included--either a side of mustard or cheese.

All in all, we would come back and try some new items and definitely order the jalapenos again.

The indoor decor is calming natural colors and wood. There were very few people when we went on a Saturday for a late lunch. They have a simple menu with inexpensive prices. Staff were wearing masks. 

I tried the beer queso nachos with pulled pork. It should have more pork for the amount of chips. The plating also impacted the quality of the nachos and messed up the toppings/chip ratio. The smaller plate meant they had to stack the nachos higher and leave extra layers of chips completely dry while top layer was overly sauced and soggy. Switching to a bigger plate would allow the nacho topping to be spread more evenly. The queso is amazing and the chips that I built to have a good topping ratio were enjoyable.

Food is incredible... had beer queso nachos and the cheese sauce on it is out of the world. Nice outdoor seating for a peaceful night. We had a late night drinks and an appetizer. Service was good, setting was nice.

The food was good, my friends and I got different burgers and we all enjoyed our meal. Gavin, our server, did a great job and continually checked up on us throughout the night. Would recommend to anyone who just wants to grab a quick bite to eat and hang out with friends.

PLATTERS!
Aside from the chicken parm being unappetizing (cardboard) and the soggy cold fries, here is the worst part of my experience. All of the platters come with fries and a small coleslaw. It is stated right there on the menu. They forgot to send the coleslaw, no big deal, right? Wrong.

We placed another order and informed them that they forgot the coleslaw for the chicken parm platter, asked them to throw it in the bag with the new delivery. They said no. "It only comes with the chicken fingers". They refused to send it. We also told them hey, the menu you just dropped off with the order also has it stated on the menu! No coleslaw for me, they refused. A tiny issue but very revealing. I also own a business, couldn't imagine doing business this way. I wish the chicken would have at least been good :-(

This is the worst cheese steak I've ever had. I ordered a mushroom cheese steak and the mushrooms were cold like they just came right out of the can. The sandwich was super small. I had quite a few sandwiches from the point breeze location and they were great. Nice long rolls plenty of meat and they all ways tasted great. The one Holmes Avenue was just horrible. Never again will go there or recommend them.

I was in the neighborhood seeing my doctor when I realized there was a Freshworks down the street.  The Freshworks in my neighborhood (The Port Richmond location) is currently being remodeled and is closed.  Since my wife and I have been jonesin for Freshworks since my location closed I got one of our favorite items: A Pizza Steak.

Gotta say, one of the worst cheesesteaks I've had.  Compared to the Freshworks in my neighborhood, they were skimpy on the meat, The bread was hard and crumbly on one side, and i honestly couldn't say if there was any cheese on it. I figured some kinda consistent quality would carry over store to store but I was wrong.

Also only 1 staff member had a mask on.  WEAR YOUR DAMN MASKS.

1 rule: CALL FIRST! Have been turned away by a note on the door many times after making a special detour. :(
That said, it is absolutely worth the detour! Amazing small business with fresh, authentic gyros and grape leaves (my go-to's) It is the best Greek I've had anywhere! :)
This food is so good, I had the falafel sandwich and fresh lemonade.  They truly live up to their name, the customer service is so awesome.

Amazing customer service and very friendly ppl! I ordered the beef gyro platter that came with a salad, and hummus. I also had a side of falafel with the Orange Passion smoothie.

The gyro was flavorful and came in a thin and crispy pita. It was very flavorful yet it wasn't heavy on me. The falafel came with a salad and was also flavorful. The smoothie wasn't overwhelming sweet and tasty. Everything was fresh and you can tell it was homemade.

I can't wait to come back!
We were craving gyros but weren't familiar with the area and we are  so glad we found Smileys's. The food was amazing and the service really did make us smile.

This is the healthiest place in Manayunk! Mark the people are very friendly and the food is always very good and delicious. I highly recommend this please at any time to anyone. My personal favorite is to take out food from Smileys and find a nice place in a park to eat it and enjoy a wonderful day.

Line is often around the corner and down the block I mean I won't butcher this review because my first experience was good and the Philly cheesesteaks are pretty decent BUT not that amazing, customer service is not the best however if you like a big sloppy philly cheesesteak definitely go here here!!! 

Sidenote the pictures below was of the Philly cheesesteak sandwich with cheese wiz the first time I came here in 2017, the second time in 2021 however it was prepared like a sloppy Joe very sloppy and soggy not the same as the first time for sure -- less meat and no pickles (major side eye !!!)

Jim's is an institution, and the long lines are a testament to its popularity. Tried their Pepper steak sandwich, and was not disappointed. They are super generous with their portion. The kitchen staff are incredibly efficient; it's like watching a symphony perform. Bread was soft but not too soggy; steak and peppers were piled high. Only gave 3/5 stars because surprisingly the steak was bland; probably because I didn't get it with cheese and wanted to taste the meat. With a little sweet relish it was a nice complement. There's also seating upstairs for a nice sit down. Overall a very nice experience; just could do with a little more seasoning in the meat.

You could get a better steak from a blind heroin addict in Salt Lake City. Bad bread, sparse meat, no flavor. Also the "heat" fries are the same thing with two spice packets. The packets are so old the spice has crustified into a rock.

This place sucks.

I remember going to Navy welding school in Philly and hitting the town with a few shipmates.  We chose South Street.  Turns out that was a good choice because I had Jim's Steaks for the first time and every philly to date has been measured against it.  So years later, and a few thousand miles of distance, I was informed of a site called Goldbelly where you can order food from anywhere in the world.  Knee-jerk reaction was to see if Jim's Steaks was participating.  They sure are.  I am cooking my last of the 4 pack I ordered.  One bite and I am warped back to my South Street experience.  Wit wiz of course.  Haters complain about using a processed cheese product on it and probably turn around and consume plant based meat substitutes that are processed even more than you think.  This or they eat an Arby's beef and cheddar sandwich without even blinking.  

Its about taste.  Of course I won't eat one of these every single day, but once in a while, when you want a real philly, do it.
Decent cheesesteak but nowhere near the best. Not worth the insanely long lines. This is middle of the road for Philly. There are a couple gems on South street alone.

Had guacamole with chips and shrimp cocktail and tacos placeros. The guac was super fresh and tasty and plenty of it and the chips were fresh made. The shrimp cocktail had a few giant shrimps around the edge like you used to get at restaurants back in the day and super fresh and several small ones in cocktail sauce. The cocktail sauce could have been a little spicier. It needed some horseradish. The only other quibble was I did not really need potatoes with my tacos placeros. The woman at the other table across from me got the molcajete and my eyes almost fell out. The waitress was super friendly. All in all great value with food that was thoughtfully prepared with premium ingredients.

Definitely a tasty and solid 4 stars. Was politely and quickly served by walking up, and received my food in under 10 minutes. 

The bag was a little on the light side, and the chorizo tacos were tasty but could have used some more filling. The salsa verde was good but a little weaker than I like, and I could have used some extra spice from another salsa option. 

With that being said it was good service and a tasty quick meal that I was craving in the moment - cost about 7.50 too

My friend David wanted to do a Taco Tuesday Night in South Philadelphia and we decided to pick San Miguelito. Man, did we choose the right place!

I showed up and upon saying "como estas" I was greeted with an abundance of Tacos and mexican dishes all for under $50 dollars.

I ordered the steak tacos and the Mexican Fajitas and my friend ordered the San Miguelito (pictured above). The meat the sides are so delicious and authentic!

Additionally, the owner was super friendly and awesome! I highly recommend the place for TakeOut and will go back!!
Top price for a regular flat steak on a plan soft roll same as wit or without, Frank's on Frankford Ave is better for the same thing.

I mean talk about a fantastic first Philly cheesesteak experience, it was tremendous. We ordered with grilled onions and American cheese. It's very filling! Also, the guys behind the counter are awesome and service was great!

Perfect spot for the perfect classic Philly cheesesteaks. Corner spot with window ordering nothing fancy but there's no fancy when it comes to original Philly cheesesteaks. Quality bread too so important! Service was quick and polite just how I like it!!

Very damn expensive for few meat slices. It's definitely a good cheese steak but not worth for the size and quantity of meat slices. I'd recommend John's roast pork, tastes better and way bigger serving for same price.
love there steaks and fries. worker always pleasant and nice people.

Hosted a 100th birthday party in the private party room at Original's this weekend, and we had a great time.  The food was delicious, the room is beautiful and very comfortable with its own entrance and restrooms, and the staff was amazing.  They really went out of their way to make the day easy and successful.  Definitely recommend Kim and her staff!

I asked for chicken cheese steak hoagie, with everything. Got a Plain chicken steak. So went back and got a second one and this time it was correct but with everything means with condiments, so got no ketchup. I wasn't going back a 3rd time, I'll take my dry sandwich home . Thanks

I've been to originals about 3 times so far since the covid restrictions were lifted. I work right down the street so the restaurant is very convenient for me to grab a bite to eat before heading home. I've tried the Caesar salad, the veggie "wrap", Buffalo shrimp & pierogies. Everything was great except for the salad, the dressing was very fishy but I'm assuming it was made with actual anchovies. I'm not big into the fishy Caesar dressing but that's just my own personal opinion! I think my favorite thing so far was the veggie wrap! It was more of a Stromboli, not gonna lie I was a little confused when it came out because I was expecting an actual sandwich wrap but it was large &delicious. You could split it with another person so I would order it again!  The two servers I had were Haley & Paul. They were extremely friendly & very attentive. All of the staff there seems friendly while I was being served another server asked if I needed anything. It was nice knowing multiple servers are paying attention to all of the tables. The outside area is by far my favorite! Such a hidden gem. Overall it's a little pricy for "bar food" but I look at it as paying for the convenience so I can't complain too much about pricing especially when the service is good! I will definitely be back.

The food here was lovely and reminded me of my time in San Sebastián and Rioja.  The duck and octopus pintxos were flavorful and well cooked.   We also enjoyed the cheese plate, and found the Spanish blue with the toasted bread to be a highlight.   The service was extremely rushed, and even though we attempted thoroughly to slow down the meal it was hard to make the entire experience last longer than an hour. If trying to mirror a meal in northern Spain, rushed service is not characteristic.

Pre-anniversary celebration with another couple. Staff was accommodating. We sat outside and sangria came right away. Started with almonds and nuts, then lamb, octopus and amazing smashed potatoes, pork sausage and ended the meal with Paella: chicken and chorizo and calamari and mussels paellas. I totally recommend both paellas. Each have a different flavor and you have to try them both. Desserts we ordered were not as memorable, but overall we had a great meal.

Cute location off of Rittenhouse Square on 20th st. Wanted yummy tapas, this Place was ok. Tinfoil had a Very Limited menu. Ordered a few things to try. The burger was ok, the ham and cheese tapas was good.  I thought it could have been better

I wanted to check this place out to satisfy a paella craving.. but if you're looking for a more traditional paella, this is not the place. However, their small plates were amazing!! I believe the menu has been down-sized, most likely due to COVID but that honestly makes it easier. The duck confit and the octopus are a must get at this location. The duck was truly paired well with the flavors and not dry at all. The octopus was so well cooked and seasoned just right. It is traditional, grilled and has a slight charred taste. Love it!! We did get the paella but as I mentioned it was not the traditional kind. They use a squid ink rice and other aioli flavors. I must say it was on the saltier side for me.. leaving me needing lots of water.. not too big a fan. 

They have outdoor seating and a small indoor space with lots of wine selections. Highly recommend for a date or evening after work. The prices are very reasonable as well!!

Been here multiple times and it's still good. The quality is there, but be warned that's a bit pricey for small tapas.

The canned tuna belly is expensive and not really worth it. The tuna is pretty good, but doesn't have much flavor. Most of the flavor comes from the 3 sauces included. The roasted red pepper and beans are pretty good. The bread is buttered and top notch.

The lamb skewers are definitely great. You get two, but these come in a plate with a great puree sauce that i loved. I considered licking the plate to clear that puree.

The paella isn't too bad. It's a bit light on the seafood for the price. I also think the seafood is cooked separately and then added at the end. None of it is dyed black in the squid ink. Maybe this is how it's made? They also add splotches of the sauce from the tuna. While good, it would be better on the side cause it's 3 different types of random sauces on different spoonfulls.

The food was always very good.  Unfortunately last night I ordered delivery thru Uber eats and the chicken was completely raw. I ate some of the butter sauce over rice and thought it tasted different and then I bit into chicken and it was completely raw.  When I called, the owner basically called me a liar, told me to text him a picture which I did, then he told me he checked the other chicken and everything was fine told me to come in for a replacement.   I ordered thru Uber eats so i didn't have to drive.  Owner was unapologetic and not customer service oriented.  
Also anytime I order for pickup, food is never ready and takes an hour after arriving for pickup.
I was sick all night from being served raw chicken and the owners response was less than stellar.  I will not be back.

This restaurant has great authentic Indian food that taste great and ia fresh. Curry goat and butter chicken have been my got to dishes with samosas as an appetizer. Be sure to order naan bread with every dish... enjoy

I ordered the mattar paneer and requested mild spice, however when I received it it was not mild, it may be just because I can't handle spice but I've ordered the same dish from Taj and it was better there. The complimentary dessert is nice and I can tell they care about customer service but next time they should consider paying attention to requested spice level a lot more.

The restaurant website allowed me to place an online order and select the time of pick up to be 4:55. I showed up to a closed restaurant saying it opens at 5. I went in at 5 to pick up my order and they said they had just started working on it, an hour later the order was ready. Several other disgruntled guests showed up to pick up there orders as well and had the same issues -- they did NOTHING to compensate for the inconvenience and the continuous promises that the order would be ready in "5 minutes" instead of telling the truth. If I could give them a negative rating I would. I will not be returning to this restaurant ever again, and would be surprised if they stay in business given the lack of customer service.

In my humble opinion Minerva is the best Indian restaurant in the New Tampa/Wesley Chapel area. The wait for an order to be filled is typically longer than others which is because of most of the dishes are made from scratch. 

You'll receive a free dessert from time to time all depending on how frequent you visit or how much you're spending. There's nothing on the menu that you can go wrong with. All dishes from the Minerva special biryani to the palak paneer are delectable.
I love their food everything tastes great! My favorites are Curry goat, oxtails, fried fish, jerk chicken & red snapper. Butt don't sleep on their soul food side, the Mac & cheese is  bomb !!

I went a few times during covid when they started the out door only pick up situation and the wait was ridiculous. Not sure if they are only doing this method, but this place always had a long wait but the food is good.

I'm Jamaican so I can't eat anybody food. The service wasn't bad or anything but I ordered the stew chicken and it wasn't it. I couldn't finish it. And me is a person weh love nyam! Can't say I'll be back.
First time eating here... I had the Jerk chicken, Ox tail, and Fried fish... all were very good. The Mac & Cheese was grandma good!  Highly recommended.

There's always a line and now I know why. Holy crap their food is good and perfectly seasoned! I wanted to try everything so I ordered the goat Curry, oxtail, and jerk chicken with a bunch of sides. EVERYTHING was on point and delicious.
Super yum! Items taste fresh and the portions were wonderful! We even sampled the frozen yogurt! Great, quick, and friendly service!

Not my favorite poke place, but they will definitely continue to have my service with their great customer service and the dole whips. 

Don't get me wrong, the poke bowls are fresh and delicious, but the bowls could have used a bit more rice. 

The dole ice cream cups are a good price and taste delicious. 

The servers are very helpful and explain everything out and even came over and gave us a sample of the dole ice cream while we were enjoying our poke. Hence why I ordered a large after we enjoyed our meal.

All I can say is WOW!  

First the gentleman that helped with the details of ALL the choices is amazing.  I would come back just because you can tell he loves this place.  So friendly and so knowledge.  I think I got healthier just listening to him talk about the food.

The options you choose from are numerous.  All bowls are $12, although there are a couple premium items they will tell you about.  Unless you crave a premium, the rest of the items are so satisfying.  Unlike other similar bowl concepts, here you get to pick THREE proteins instead of what is normally one.  Or you can double or triple up on your favorite.  I did ahi tuna, salmon and shrimp.  Then so many toppings I added that I won't even mention (you can see how colorful my bowl picture is).

And then you HAVE to get a pineapple Dole whip for dessert.  They are huge, so you can definitely split one if there are two if you.  I had so much in mine that I took half home and ate it later.

Plenty of seating inside when visiting on a Saturday night at 8pm.  Lot of people were getting takeout.

Parking is endless and close to the retail strip center storefront.  This is right beside a Winn Dixie (which had a liquor store) if you need to shop afterwards.

I highly recommend this place.  Look for a check-in here on Yelp for 10% off an entree or I've also seen coupons in the neighborhood coupon flyer for a free dole whip.  Support this place or it will disappear!

Rachel was amazing! She carefully made my complicated order with marked up menus and crossed out everywhere. She was personable and I felt like she cared about the company and her customers. She marked each bowl so we could find ours with ease and she even threw in extra crunchies on top! It's my first time here but I will definitely be going back. Highly recommend also food was delicious and fresh!

This restaurant is in a plaza by the wendixi market. It caught my eye because I've never had poke before. I ordered a bowl of mixed protein raw tuna and chicken with some brown rice and exotic flavors of toppings. This place is extremely clean and the food is delicious. I just think it's overpriced with the portion on the food and double meat is expensive. I understand that double meat is extra but didn't expect them to tell me 6-7 dollars more. The staff were really good at explaining what toppings and gave me some great suggestions. Thanks and good luck

Wonderful wonderful service! The vibe here was sooo warm and welcoming. The hostess/waitress Chris was amazing and so accommodating. We had the fried pickles for appetizer and they were delicious! I had their take on whiskey sour..8/10. My friend tried a few of the local draft on tap and she was also pleased. Great place for happy hour. Loved the atmosphere I definitely will return.
Great service, great food. They were super patient with our toddler. I know this is weird to say but their buns are delicious so get the burger or chicken sandwich. And the fries are perfect.
Great place.  Friendly service, beautiful restored interior and great food and beer.  I highly recommend the brussel sprouts.  Top notch sprouts!
Best take out burger I've had in Philly so far! Soooooo good. Can't recommend enough. I can see myself becoming a regular here.

The food here was great. I had the burger and ordered the Brussel sprouts, which was delicious. My boyfriend, friend and I really enjoyed the food. Also the costumer service was great. I would definitely come back.

DONT COME HERE went to the door at 8:02 am they never answered So I thought they were closed  But they open at 5 AM and I work at a restaurant myself so it doesn't matter if you have two or even three people on the line the doors are SUPPOSED to be open. once i see they were serving drive thru the black lady on the inside just gives me an ugly look when i simply knocked on the window to see what was going on. I haven't even ate and I already don't like this place. but then I saw the reviews and they all say the same thing I'm saying so it's no surprise sadly. would never recommend. Needs a different manager and crew. Either that or shut the place down cause it's not being run right.

Waited 5 min so they can take my order and  20 to get my order people behind me left cause it took long. They need more staff or new management cause service sux big time and they didn't seem to care when I complain. Great another cold lunch

When do the drive-through nobody answered had to pull up front and knock on the door in the window three times the lady looked at me didn't even answer the door finally answered the drive-through and said I'll be with you in one minute after 15 min. Asked for fresh french fries because the new the french fries have been sitting there still got french fries I have been re-dropped horrible business

This location is awful!! I have been working in this area for 4 years and everyone in my office cannot stand this location.  The food is cold, Or you get the wrong food, Wrong Bill, not all of your food in the bag etc.  The window people are always in a hurry and are never nice!!! There is no efforet i can tell you that.  Nothing like waiting in a line order and your burger is so cold the cheese slices are hard.

tl;dr pretty expensive, and maybe some growing pains

We had a nice dinner at the Black Squirrel a few nights ago. For some reason the door next to the hostess is locked, which I learned when I tried it and couldn't get in, only to come in and hear the people at the bar loudly talking about me trying it and not getting in. Felt a little embarrassed. While I was talking to the hostess, a woman tried the door - still locked. We sat outside and watched a few other groups try the door. No one wanted to try the unlocked door because the door handle was broken and hanging by a screw. I'm not sure why they didn't have a sign. Maybe they do now?

They have a nice selection of English and local beers. The cocktail menu looks fantastic. The food menu is short, but everything is good. $22 for a single piece of fish and a cup of chips is a pretty wild price. Not even any smashed peas. I won't order it again if we go back. My wife liked her Chicken dish well enough. All in all, this place seems way more expensive than it needs to be, and makes me miss the Falls Taproom even more. The decor is cute, but the "elevated" vibe seems to only apply to the prices, everything in the restaurant looked second hand and the wait staff were wearing t-shirts.

We probably won't go back, but it seems popular, so that's good for the neighborhood!

Fantastic meal.  Had the chicken tikka and fish $ chips for mains, definitely top 3 around PHL.  The tandoori wings were tremendous!  Amazing service from Ray and Gordon.  A+ experience all around, highly recommend!

Before reviewing it's fair to say that the Black Squirrel is newly opened and  from what I've heard it is associated with two other eating establishments in East Falls which I have patronized. The cocktails were great. My companion and I tried their version of an old fashioned, fabulous. There was a wide selection of entrees, but since it was a hot and humid afternoon, we decided on apps only. Their rendition of classic French onion soup was original and good. The other apps we ordered and shared were equally as good. Ordered a crab cake sandwich to go for husband. The whole experience was great, food wise. Except my experience sitting on an old previously purposed chair that collapsed.  Btw, I am weight and height appropriate. Fortunately I wasn't hurt, but that is this restaurant's theme of using repurposed chairs, dinnerware and tables. I support the theme, but their quality control process for old chairs is suspect. My ego was a little tattered as restaurant was full of customers. No manager came to check on my well being. The only thing comped was the to-go crab cake sandwich. One would think the broken old chair would warrant a comped meal for me and my guest. After leaving we both had feelings the restaurant thought we were to blame for the chair failure, especially since I
called the next day asking to speak with the Manager. Needless to say the call was not returned. Chair experience reduces rating by 2 stars.

Went here for an early dinner and was blown away by the creative drinks and food not mention unique dinning room experience. So happy this place opened adding a creative spin to the restaurant scene in Manayunk and East Falls.

Great beer for great prices. Could almost stop the review there. The cocktails are good and are all made with fresh fruit. The food was good and unique. Looking forward to them having specials and deserts. Will come back for the beer and grab a bite while I drink

Bring a blanket and pillow.. they take forever.
Sandwich is good. But the wait is like a lifetime

My Fam went to Koch's about 6yrs ago. I wish I could remember his name
So outgoing. So lively. He was doing several things at once  giving us samples of his food. This place Was Delicious! 
Untill my boyfriend wanted to make me happy
THIS WAS THE WORST RUBEN I EVER HAD!!!!
I reminded him that I have been there several years ago and I was so happy with it, that  I came back again. 
I am going to just fast forward to the end of what happened. I was so upset so so so very upset when I opened that sandwich. It wasn't Grilled. It was not even warm. The Ruben was 75% sauerkraut. The bottom slice of rye bread was so soggy. There was only about 10% of corned beef on there. 
This sandwich was supposed to be HUGE browns it up it cost about $15. Not to mention that when we got to unwrap the sandwich we were salivating for....was Terrible! 
It bothered me so much I made my boyfriend go back to the deli. We wrapped it up and were ready to give it back.
I had to get in line again because of the Covid. It is a very very very small little deli. So I didn't mind. Put my mask on walked up to the door. The guy that was at the door asked me what was wrong so I told him. He told The guy making the food. Then, OMG!! The nice guy started screaming " What did you order? What did you order? I am make whatever you ordered!" 
He went crazy. 
I wanted my money back. I stood my ground, and I got my money back.
(Also bought some chicken liver salad. That went bad the very next day.)
I won't spend $15 for a sandwich of sauerkraut on rye bread. He continued yelling at me, and I just had to walk away.

We decided to try a new place for dinner and regret it! The gentleman who took my order was friendly, but he had a difficult time understanding me. Perhaps this caused some of the issues that occurred with errors to the order. When I finished ordering, he told me the total due and said the food should be here in 45 minutes. One hour later the food arrived cold. The delivery person told me the amount due and it was $5 more than I was told on the phone by the owner, Mel. I called the store and was told that the price changed because Mel forgot to include the cost for the chicken parm. 
I was looking over the receipt and saw that we were charged $16.75 for the chicken parm meal. We wouldn't have minded paying that if it was actually good. However, the spaghetti had no sauce other than what was put on the chicken and the chicken was so overcooked that the ends were hard and inedible. There was also very little cheese even though we paid for extra. 
I called to find out more information about why we were charged that price. The receipt was confusing since it broke it down into separate charges. Mel, the owner, proceeded to tell me that the $10,25 was for the spaghetti and the $5.50 was for the chicken. He felt the price was great for the amount of food. I explained that it is a lot to pay for something that isn't good. I was then told in a not so friendly way that I shouldn't order from there again. No problem, Mel!
The best food around for 40 years pizza and cheesesteak are the bomb the wings are great and salad and hoagies are healthy
This is one of my favorite spots. I order from there at least once a week. Great service and even better food. Can't go wrong with anything on the menu.

This place is awesome. I love their food but srsly getting delivery from them can be rough. Idk if I'm that hard to understand? I need to record myself normally placing an order and upload it for Yelpers to comment. Every time I order it's a fight to get it to me. 

I also think I've been lied to more than once that the driver was on their way. 

But anyway the food is good. No break out items. Anytime the guys and I order we all share so I've had some of everything. 

Have you e we had a pizza with ground beef and onions? Me neither but a coworker said that's what he wanted and they made it no questions asked.

When have shorts and f'n Hawaiian shirts been considered casual dress?!?!! 

I was excited to try somewhere new. Sorta dressy but not really.  Jeans and a collared shirt? I can do that. 

Dudes wearing short ass shorts and Hawaiian shorts? Are you kidding me?!!!!

I normally don't care about something like this but I chose this place because it was a little more upscale than chili's! What the actual f?

The vibe? Besides Richard wearing shorts, it was really cool. I'd come back. 

Food? Amazing. Had the sea bass. It was killer!!!

Drinks?  Ehhh. So so. The one thing going for this place in the drink category is that they are not expensive. I could swear the first old fashioned that came out was NOT smoked and sat at the bar for a while. Still....not terrible.  Eventually I had a decent smoked old fashioned after switching up the whiskey. I love redemption, but it wasn't working here. 

To wrap it up, I'll be back. 
I'm pissed there is a dress code that is not at all enforced.  
The food was great. Can't wait to try more!

To the guy in shorts, get the F out!

We went to see a friend sing and play the keyboard-superb by the way Allen-and we were pleasantly surprised by the food and service! Ask for Dominic and definitely order the crab cakes for apps!!! Allen performs Thursday through Saturday 6-9ish...CHECK IT OUT FOR SURE!!!
Food was amazing, service was amazing and restaurant was amazing inside I def recommend coming with your significant other here!
Very good. The food was good as was the service. Atmosphere was comfortable as well. A little pricey, but we all enjoyed it.

My wife and absolutely love the food here. The problem I see is at the bar. They get so busy that there is no place to walk up and order a drink while you are waiting for your table. Also the service at the bar is not welcoming. If you do not like your job, then I suggest you find something better suited for your lack of a warm inviting and friendly reception. We took our best friends couple there last night and had a wonderful sit down experience. Drinks were delicious and the food was perfect. Service was on point. Thank you, please work on your bartenders.

Not great food. Had to send a burger back due to they tried to serve it with cheese they scraped off and a family member has a dairy allergy. All fries were cold and sent back. Took a long time to replace burger and fries. Our server was nice. Sauces were okay. Won't go back though.  Nothing special here.

Head a pick up order that was just sitting on the counter behind the register for 20 minutes. Bad system just put the to go orders where customers can pick them up.  Oneslow as can be kid working the register with the big biggest mask I have ever seen in my life covering his entire face including his eyes
Very friendly staff. Very quick to bring the food out. My burger was delicious! I will definitely be coming back here.

Came to this location after getting my nails done right next door and right off the bat I was super uncomfortable. The guy at the register couldn't meet my eyes as I was ordering he was staring at my chest and I was wearing a normal t-shirt and not exposed..second issue, my bf ordered after me and had repeated his order twice. He got a burger with an egg on it. The kid at the register had him repeat the order 3 times. We paid and sat at our table, no problem. When my bf burger came out it had no egg on it even though he repeated himself three times to the kid up front. Ok, no worries, things happen. Well, he lets the girl who works there know it's missing his egg, turns out the kid didn't even ring it up when taking his order. On top of them F*cling up my bf order, the waitress came back out and asked him to pay for the egg so my bf got up and paid the $1.25 for a F*cking egg that was supposed to be over easy and the yolk was cooked all the way through. Honestly burger 21 if you're hurting for a dollar and 25 cents after you made the mistake 2x , don't you think as a company, your customer service would matter? I'm not typically the person who makes a fuss or is a Karen when mistakes happen, but damn. WEAK service and lazy employees. Maybe that's why it always seems to be empty inside your restaurant? This was a disappointment of the highest regard. $10 for a burger is WAY too much to deal with this bs

Wow the guy who made the shakes took literally years to make my shake. Looks like he was just having a jolly old time making me wait forever. The fries were sub par too. Lucky I don't put one star. I'll prob def never come to this location but maybe  the other one to give it one more chance. Thank you for reading
I love it when an establishment's entire menu is appealing as I found at Rybrew.  Great to have so many fresh bread choices.  The drink selections are the best!
What a treasure. Fresh and original in the menu choices. Great smiling staff. The selection of beers and other is impressive. Worth finding and traveling to.
The Panini's were good as hell, I have to admit the best ones I've had in Philly. That Veggie pesto one was excellent, will def be back

Ordered two salads and their daily soup as take out- very tasty and generous portions! They have lots of good options on their menu. We will definitely be returning to try more items! They also have a good beer and seltzer selection in store. Definitely recommend!

My husband and I popped by Rybrew today while we were in the area. There were several people waiting outside for sandwiches, and once inside the phone was ringing with orders as well! 

My husband had a crab cake sandwich that he enjoyed, and I had the roast beef and cheddar sandwich which was absolutely delicious. I asked for the horseradish mayo on the side and I loved it! 

Rybrew peeps, there's some retail space on Washington Ave in Graduate Hospital. Just saying!

The injera was as thin as paper and wasn't the normal color of injera. It makes me wonder if they even use teff flour, it tastes like it's made with all purpose flour and tasted old.

The combo dish was $18 but was in total less than a cup of food. 

The shiro was bland, the gomen alright but the yemisir wat was really good.

Overall, not worth it for the price at all, and was the most disappointing experience I've ever had at an Ethiopian restaurant -- and Ethiopian food is my favorite cuisine
So spot on. Great food and cultural experience. Amazing staff. Been around forever and it's worth the visit.

Love this place.  Don't know where to start but I would say try the cinnamon bun (it's big and delicious). The breakfast is done well with the taste of small delicious kitchen cooking that makes your day.  I would also be remiss in not mentioning the bbq.  Do yourself a favor and have some.

Cute little corner brunch place in suburbs of Fishtown! The area was quiet and weather was so nice for outdoor seating. My friend and I got the chicken&waffle and eggs benedict with fried chicken as a substitute from the ham that comes with it! Def recommend the fried chicken instead. The chicken is crispy! Not the most tender but it was still delicious! Waffle was crispy on the outside as well. Reminded me of the Popeyes chicken. 

They took a while for the food to come out and service was a bit slow bc it was a bit busy but other than that food was delishhh! My friend also enjoyed the americano:)

It is really nice place for breakfast. We got streak&eggs and biscuits gravy which is really yummy. The service is excellent and attentive. Totally recommended this place and definitely gonna come back soon.

This doesn't feel even remotely like the same Butcher Bar from a couple years ago. I've had multiple rave-worthy experiences here previously but the most recent visit was so disappointing. Other than the drinks (which were great!) everything we ordered was just not good. The charcuterie board we got at the beginning was really off putting - plus the woman running the food said that typically she'd explain the meat/cheeses but she didn't have time?

We got a couple of mains and sides as well which were not near noteworthy. The whole experience was just kind of weird and not worth the time or price tag. 

Our server and the hostess were both very kind and this could still be a solid place to grab a few drinks but like I said, it's not the same dining experience it once was. Hoping they figure it out because this was a go-to spot for many pre-covid.

Absolutely loved my boar ribs, which were amazingly tender with the meat literally falling off the bone. The Butcher cheese board and old fashions were spot on. Their portions were also very good- not too much, not too little. Highly recommend if you're in the mood for meat.

Went for dinner a couple months ago, went in with a plan to try certain items. Confit ducks wings were solid. The brussel sprouts and cauliflower mixture could have used more time in the oven. The roasted portabellos were my personal fave, the Korean short ribs were tender and had a nice spice profile. The meatballs looked moist at first and one even squirted hot liquid but sadly they were dry. They were out of the key lime parfait so we split the German chocolate cake in which my partner told me how the name of the cake came to be and it you ever wondered its not because of coconut; which FYI there wasn't any on this cake so clearly identity issues but because the creators last name was German like just German. The cake itself was very underwhelming and not moist at all. Tasted like a bad box.

From the butchers Butcher Board to the delicious Smoked Wild Boar Ribs & their infamous Royale with Cheese Sandwich, I will honestly say it's a must! 

STEVE the bartender brought us one of the best experiences, friendly, knowledgeable, and extremely talented with his bartending skills! 

Please give this place a try! It's 5/5!

Sad we couldn't order the meat board. We didn't know you needed to order in advance. Every dish we ordered was great! The monkey bread and lamb were delicious. The side of Gouda Mac was a meal! I've never seen bacon like this! Service was wonderful too! 

Only negative- didn't enjoy sitting at a picnic table. Uncomfortable with a dress! And it was raining therefore you get wet!

This restaurant t is filthy dirty.  The people working there were dirty too.  They got my order wrong and I had to go back to get it corrected.  
It was my first time to an Einstein Bagel.
They need to get it together!

Had lunch here... and it was pretty darned good! Great guacamole. So tasty, in fact, we ordered take out for later. Unfortunately they missed an item in our to-go bag. But the manager was super friendly on the phone & fixed it up for next time. We'll definitely visit again. 

They have indoor & outdoor seating, some vegan options. Worth a lunch stop if you're over by the museum area.
I went here recently. I had the fish tacos and the Agua Fresca. Both delicious! Highly recommend!

I loved this place! would recommend. my crispy beer battered fish tacos with the chipotle remoulade were great. atmosphere was comfortable and friendly. servers were nice. sauce selection was good. 

taco spot with a beach, surfer vibe in the middle of philly. enjoyed the experience.

We used to get their fish tacos a lot when we lived in the neighborhood. Came back after few years and were disappointed by most of the foods we tried. Battered fish tacos were good, but the shrimp chorizo tacos were too salty. Chorizo was one note just salty. The side of plantains was decent, but the rice and beans weren't flavorful.
